tracker.summary: The BLE/tracker path is a four-layer pipeline with strict one-way dependencies: `src/ble/` (transport, the only place a BLE library is imported) → `src/protocol/` (adapter + pure decoder + stream orchestration) → `src/domain/punch|programs|workout` (normalized events, capability tier, matching) → `src/storage/` (SQLite). A glove's indication on `ca281069` is stamped with `performance.now()` inside the native ble-plx callback, written to the capture sink BEFORE any parsing, then split into 9-byte records by `FightCampV1Decoder` and emitted as `TrackerPunchEvent`s. The decoder is byte-level CONFIRMED (H11, from the decompiled Hykso APK) but deliberately refuses to classify technique (H12 settled it on hardware), so the capability tier is pinned at `hand-timestamp` and all cue scoring is hand-sequence-only. The whole stack is well-commented and unusually honest about what it cannot claim. The two biggest live risks are documentation drift — the single most important operational fact (trackers MUST be bonded) exists only in Kyle's memory file, never in `docs/protocol/hypotheses.md`, and the proven meaning of `ca281070` contradicts its name in code — plus a genuine time-base mix in `CueMatcher` where epoch-ms tracker timestamps are sorted and offset against `performance.now()` monotonic values.

keyFiles.role: The decoder. Pure, no I/O. `decodeFrame(frame, state)` → `{events, malformed, unknown, notes}`. Owns record splitting, the velocity piecewise curve, the epoch+subsecond timestamp math, the `recovered` backfill test, and `mapType()` which ALWAYS returns 'unknown'.
All UUIDs and mode-command byte tables, transcribed from Hykso `m1/C0477c.java` and `m1/AbstractC0475a.java`. Also `buildClockSyncBytes(nowMs)` (5 bytes: LE u32 epoch seconds + one subsecond byte).

Implements `TrackerProtocolAdapter`. `buildInitializationPlan` is the 8-step Hykso start-session sequence (clock sync FIRST, then 3 subscribes, device-info read, mode-normal, hand assign, command 17). Also scoreAdvertisement / inspectGatt / start / stop / sleep.

Per-device orchestrator. Snapshots GATT, walks the init plan op by op through the facade, stamps `handAtCapture` on every frame, then calls `adapter.decodeFrame`. Collects `initErrors[]` and `deviceInfo{}` into a `PunchStreamController`.

Implements the domain `PunchEventSource` port over `PunchStream`, one stream per hand slot. Arms only when the radio confirms connected; re-arms on the `ready`/`streaming` transition; re-stamps `hand` from the slot on the way out. Declares `FIGHTCAMP_V1_SOURCE_CAPABILITY`.

App-wide singleton: one `TrackerPunchEventSource` for both known gloves for the app's whole life, plus a 20 s heartbeat that re-writes mode-normal and reads battery. Exists because a silent central makes the glove hang up.

820 lines, the only file importing `@sfourdrinier/react-native-ble-plx` (v3.9.3). `monitorCharacteristic` (line 500) builds the `RawBleFrame` and calls `frameSink.capture()` before `onFrame()`. `connect()` (line 302) requests Balanced priority and adopts errorCode 203.
The only BLE surface the rest of the app may depend on. Interface + `registerBleManagerFactory` / `getBleManager` singleton. Documents the persist-before-parse and `setupOutcome` contracts.
The hard-coded hand assignment. Two trackers, fixed addresses, fixed hands. This is where `hand` actually comes from — never the payload.

489 lines of hard-won connect strategy: permissions gate, native-truth probe, evict-then-scan, SERIAL connects, direct attempt for gloves the scan missed, 5-attempt retry budget, suspend during workouts. The header explains why the scan must NOT be removed.
The authoritative (batch) matcher. Greedy, event-time ordered, earliest-unfilled slot. `gate: 'window' | 'open'`. Hand mismatch becomes an extra, not an assignment (D18).

Streaming adapter: provisional per-punch feedback + authoritative settle on window close, with `corrections[]` when they disagree. Owns the cue-id-keyed open slot that fixed the 2026-08-31 orphaned-matcher bug.
The single place that decides how much may be scored. `resolveCapabilityTier` + `sequenceScoreLabel` + `tierScoresTechnique`. FightCamp v1 lands on `hand-timestamp`.

The additive-only form bonus built on H12's device-LOCAL byte profiles. `H12_DEVICE_PROFILES` holds only bytes that discriminate exactly one family per device. Agreement adds, disagreement never subtracts.

The concrete `CaptureSink`. Two `FrameBuffer`s (raw frames, decoded events), batch 25 / 1 s latency / 2000 cap, address→surrogate-key cache. `stop()` releases the capture id synchronously before the async drain — a deliberate fix for 19 orphaned punch events.
`punch_events` table + the compound dedup unique index. Marked SHIPPED — do not edit.
`cue_results` table, `CUE_OUTCOMES`, and the frozen comment that `type-mismatch` is unreachable and `expected_type` is always NULL on this hardware.
297 lines, the H-number registry: H01-H12 plus H07-REVISED. The primary source of truth for protocol claims — and the file that is now stale on three points (see gotchas).
The one committed replay fixture (2026-08-23T01:50:07Z, device EA:69:2D:9C:FD:53). Decoder tests iterate it and assert >= 22 events with all-numeric timestamps.
Decides tracker vs simulator. Latched on first render except for an idle-phase upgrade. Attaches to the keepalive source rather than building a second one (the one-stream-per-device rule).

keyConcepts.name: FIGHTCAMP_SERVICE_UUID
keyConcepts.detail: 'ca280069-5470-4e34-94dd-caf160200b29' — the custom primary service. `scoreAdvertisement` returns 100 on a UUID match, 60 on a name starting with 'fightcam' (H01: the local name is truncated to 8 chars, "FightCam").

keyConcepts.name: CHAR table (10 custom characteristics)
keyConcepts.detail: DATA_STREAM 'ca281069' (indication, the ONLY characteristic the decoder accepts frames from); COMMAND1 'ca281071'; COMMAND2 'ca281072'; DEVICE_INFO_READ 'ca281070'; NOTIFY_STATUS 'ca281073'; CONFIG_1074/1075/1076; COMMAND_ACK 'ca281078'; CLOCK_SYNC 'ca281079' (aliased as LEGACY_COMMAND — same UUID, two names). All suffixed '-5470-4e34-94dd-caf160200b29'.

keyConcepts.name: MODE_COMMAND_1_BYTES
keyConcepts.detail: Single-byte payloads for COMMAND1 (ca281071): idle 0, normal 1, gym 2, fetch 3, test 4, normalKick 5, shutdown 15, unnamed16 16, unnamed17 17, unnamed18 18. Writing `normal` (1) is what enables the punch stream AND what drains the tracker's buffered punches.

keyConcepts.name: MODE_COMMAND_2_BYTES + hand assignment
keyConcepts.detail: zero 0, one 1, two 2. The init plan writes right → `one` (1), left → `two` (2) to COMMAND2, reproducing Hykso `j1/e.java` :g() → C0477c.b(position) where position 1 = right, 2 = left. Omitted entirely when `ctx.hand` is absent.

keyConcepts.name: Initialization plan order (8 ops)
keyConcepts.detail: 1) write CLOCK_SYNC ca281079 (without it the tracker sits connected and idle and NEVER emits punch frames), 2) subscribe DATA_STREAM ca281069 'indication', 3) subscribe NOTIFY_STATUS ca281073 'notification', 4) subscribe COMMAND_ACK ca281078 'indication', 5) read DEVICE_INFO_READ ca281070, 6) write COMMAND1 = 0x01 mode-normal, 7) write COMMAND2 = hand byte, 8) write COMMAND1 = 0x11 (17, unnamed even in Hykso's debug map). Steps 7-8 are what stop the glove hanging up on a still hand within minutes (observed 2026-08-29).

keyConcepts.name: Record width switch
keyConcepts.detail: `const recordWidth = state.firmwareMajorVersion >= 4 ? 9 : 13`. Payload length not a nonzero multiple of the width → `{events: [], malformed: true}` with a note. Never throws.

keyConcepts.name: 9-byte record layout (v>=4)
keyConcepts.detail: byte[0] punchTypeRaw u8; byte[1..2] accelerationRaw u16 LE (`b1 | (b2 << 8)`); byte[3..6] epochSeconds u32 LE, built in floating point as `b3 + b4*0x100 + b5*0x10000 + b6*0x1000000` to stay UNSIGNED past 2038; byte[7] subSecondByte; byte[8] velocityByteRaw. `trackerTimestampMs = epochSeconds * 1000 + Math.floor((subSecondByte * 1000) / 256)` → 3.9 ms quantization.

keyConcepts.name: 13-byte record layout (v<4, legacy)
keyConcepts.detail: byte[0] type; byte[1] unused; byte[2..3] accel u16 LE; byte[4..7] epochSeconds; byte[8] subSecond; byte[9..10] unused; byte[11] velocity (plain `raw/2`, NO piecewise, NO ×1.7); byte[12] unused. Dead in practice — every probed tracker reports v>=4.

keyConcepts.name: Velocity piecewise curve
keyConcepts.detail: `v = velocityByteRaw / 2`; if v <= 4 → `v * 0.5`; elif v <= 8 → `(v - 4) * 3 + 2`; else → `(v - 8) * 6 + 14`. Then if `punchTypeRaw === 1 || punchTypeRaw === 2` → `velocity *= 1.7`. `velocityRaw` is the RAW BYTE (not raw/2, despite H11's implication text); `velocityCalibrated` is the post-curve value. `velocityUnit` is ALWAYS 'tracker-unit'.

keyConcepts.name: BACKFILL_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_000
keyConcepts.detail: `isBackfilled()` sets `recovered: true` when `Date.parse(frame.wallTimeIso) - trackerTimestampMs > 3000`. Undecidable cases (no device timestamp, unparseable arrival time) stay LIVE on purpose. Measured drains arrived 22-66 s late.

keyConcepts.name: DECODER_ID / DECODER_VERSION
keyConcepts.detail: 'fightcamp-v1' / '1.0.0'. Stamped on every event and carried into `punch_events.decoder_id/decoder_version` and `cue_results.decoder_version` so a stored session stays recalculable.

keyConcepts.name: Event id derivation
keyConcepts.detail: `TrackerPunchEvent.id = `${frame.id}-r${i}`` where `RawBleFrame.id = `${captureId}-${seq}``. `ble_frames.id` is the PRIMARY KEY, so ids must be unique ACROSS app runs — which is why frames tagged 'ephemeral' (sequence restarts at 0 each launch) must not be persisted.

keyConcepts.name: KNOWN_TRACKERS (hand assignment, hard-coded)
keyConcepts.detail: `{address: 'D7:34:B4:27:D5:84', hand: 'left', color: 'blue', displayName: 'L Punch'}` and `{address: 'EA:69:2D:9C:FD:53', hand: 'right', color: 'red', displayName: 'R Punch'}`. Compared case-insensitively via `normalize()`. Viable only because Android reports the MAC and these units do NOT use resolvable private addresses.

keyConcepts.name: Hand is never in the payload
keyConcepts.detail: H11: Hykso tracks L/R by MAC in SharedPreferences (`left_device_addr`/`right_device_addr`) and injects EXTRA_POSITION. Here `hand` is stamped three times on the way out: `PunchStream.onFrame` sets `handAtCapture` (PunchStream.ts:75), the decoder forwards `frame.handAtCapture` (Decoder.ts:139), and `TrackerPunchEventSource.deliver` re-applies the slot hand (line 329-330).

keyConcepts.name: Capability tier: hand-timestamp
keyConcepts.detail: `FIGHTCAMP_V1_SOURCE_CAPABILITY = {hand: true, timestamp: true, punchType: 'none', velocity: true}` → `tierFor` returns 'hand-timestamp'. `sequenceScoreLabel('hand-timestamp')` → 'hand-sequence match'; only 'hand-distinct-type' earns 'technique match'. `tierScoresTechnique` is false, so `CueMatcher.outcomeFor` returns 'matched' on any correct hand and 'type-mismatch' is unreachable.

keyConcepts.name: CAPABILITY_SAMPLE_SIZE = 20
keyConcepts.detail: `observedCapability()` resolves the tier from up to 20 observed events as a reality check against the declared capability. On FightCamp v1 both agree at 'hand-timestamp'; an empty sample resolves to 'hand-only'.

keyConcepts.name: HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 20_000 / MODE_NORMAL_BASE64 = 'AQ=='
keyConcepts.detail: Every 20 s the keepalive writes byte 0x01 to COMMAND1 for each connected glove, then reads battery (0x180f / 0x2a19, one byte = percent). An armed stream alone was not enough (~2 min), periodic READS were not enough (~3-5 min) — the firmware's idle timer wants inbound WRITES.

keyConcepts.name: ConnectionPriority.Balanced (never High on two links)
keyConcepts.detail: Requesting High on BOTH glove links asks this MediaTek LE scheduler for two 11-15 ms intervals it cannot service and it sheds the newer link — 'the second glove always dies' (2026-08-29). The documented revisit is High during ONE glove's init only, released after.

keyConcepts.name: errorCode 203 = adopt, don't fail
keyConcepts.detail: ble-plx 'already connected' means this app's OWN native link survived a Metro reload while JS forgot it. `connect()` bumps the generation, re-wires the disconnect watch, and returns `state: 'ready'`. Treating it as an error caused an endless connect/cancel loop. Separately: a connect TIMEOUT surfaces as 'Operation was cancelled' (errorCode 2) — compare `durationMs` against the timeout to tell them apart.

keyConcepts.name: SETUP_OUTCOME_QUIET_MS = 800
keyConcepts.detail: `SubscriptionHandle.result.success` may be optimistically true; `handle.setupOutcome` resolves on the FIRST ble-plx callback (error → failure) or settles optimistically after 800 ms of quiet. `PunchStream` awaits `setupOutcome`, which is how a silently-failed CCCD write is detected.

keyConcepts.name: Auto-connect constants
keyConcepts.detail: `AUTO_RETRY_BUDGET = 5`, `RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5_000`, default scan `timeoutMs` 10_000 in `runAutoConnect` (facade defaults: `DEFAULT_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000`, `DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`). `THIS_SESSION_STATES` = connecting, bonding, discovering, initializing, ready, streaming, recovering — a slot in any of these with native confirmation is untouchable.

keyConcepts.name: The scan is load-bearing (address type)
keyConcepts.detail: Both trackers use random-static addresses (top two bits 0b11). rxandroidble resolves an address STRING via `BluetoothAdapter.getRemoteDevice(String)`, which assumes PUBLIC — so without a scan result or a bond the connect is aimed at the wrong address type: direct connects time out and `autoConnect` parks on the accept list forever. Tried and reverted 2026-08-29. But connecting is NOT gated on the scan: an unseen known tracker still gets one direct attempt, because a bonded glove may advertise DIRECTED at its partner.

keyConcepts.name: Cue window overlap = DEFAULT_GRACE_BEFORE_MS 200
keyConcepts.detail: `DEFAULT_GRACE_BEFORE_MS = 200`, `DEFAULT_GRACE_AFTER_MS = 350`. Consecutive cue windows OVERLAP by 200 ms, so the engine emits `cue-window-opened(N)` BEFORE `cue-window-closed(P)`. `LiveCueMatcher.onCueEvent` is cue-id-keyed for exactly this reason — the unkeyed version silently discarded P and orphaned the matcher for the rest of the round.

keyConcepts.name: D18 — a wrong hand does not consume the ordinal
keyConcepts.detail: Both matchers publish a hand-mismatch punch as an extra carrying `reason: 'hand-mismatch'` and leave the slot open. Previously the index was filled before the hand was examined, which made set completion permanently unreachable after one hand error and turned a recoverable mistake into a guaranteed timeout.

keyConcepts.name: gate: 'open' vs 'window'
keyConcepts.detail: `LiveCueMatcher.settle()` calls `matcher.match(cue, events, {gate: 'open'})` because `open.events` are already exactly the punches that arrived while the window was open. Re-testing their times would apply a stricter rule than the live pass and report a correction on every punch. The two passes MUST agree — `correctionsFor` diffs them and every mismatch is logged as `puncheokie.match.corrected`.

keyConcepts.name: H12_DEVICE_PROFILES (the form bonus)
keyConcepts.detail: EA:69:2D:9C:FD:53 ('red / right'): `{2: 'hook', 3: 'straight'}`, sampleSize 42. D7:34:B4:27:D5:84 ('blue / left'): `{3: 'uppercut'}`, sampleSize 47. Both `provisional: true`, `capturedAt: '2026-08-23'`. Only bytes mapping to exactly ONE family per device are listed — byte 4 on red and byte 1 on blue are modal for several families and are deliberately omitted. `TYPE_PROFILE_VERSION = '1.0.0'`, `FORM_BONUS_PER_AGREEMENT = 1`. Agreement adds; there is no branch that subtracts.

keyConcepts.name: Capture buffer policy
keyConcepts.detail: `FRAME_BATCH_SIZE = 25`, `FRAME_MAX_LATENCY_MS = 1_000`, `FRAME_MAX_BUFFERED = 2_000`, `TICK_INTERVAL_MS = 500`. A failed flush requeues at the FRONT (ordering survives); overflow drops the OLDEST and shouts via `capture.frames.dropped`.

keyConcepts.name: punch_events dedup index
keyConcepts.detail: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_punch_events_dedup ON punch_events(COALESCE(device_address,''), COALESCE(tracker_timestamp_ms,-1), COALESCE(punch_type_raw,-1), COALESCE(velocity_raw,-1))`. FightCamp v1 carries no sequence number, so identity is this compound key. All inserts use INSERT OR IGNORE; `inserted` is derived from a `total_changes` delta because OR IGNORE reports success for a silently dropped row. Migration 008 added `acceleration_raw` and deliberately did NOT add it to the index.

keyConcepts.name: cue_results primary key
keyConcepts.detail: After migration 005: `PRIMARY KEY (session_id, generated_workout_id, block_id, repeat_index, token_index)` — `repeat_index` was added because a repeated block runs the same token indexes more than once. `observed_event_id` is a real FK into `punch_events(id)` with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, so `persistWorkoutSession` writes the named punches FIRST inside the same transaction or the whole session rolls back.

keyConcepts.name: Migration list (8, all applied in order)
keyConcepts.detail: 001_initial (tracker_devices, ble_captures, ble_frames, gatt_inventory), 002_punch_events, 003_sessions, 004_workouts (cue_results), 005_cue_result_repeat_index, 006_app_settings, 007_workout_runs, 008_punch_acceleration. 002 and 004 are marked 'SHIPPED — do not edit'.

keyConcepts.name: BLE permissions
keyConcepts.detail: API >= 31: BLUETOOTH_SCAN + BLUETOOTH_CONNECT (neverForLocation). API < 31: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION. `runAutoConnect` gates every scan on these — a scan without them silently finds nothing, which looks exactly like 'trackers won't connect' with no error anywhere. `adb uninstall` wipes prior grants.

keyConcepts.name: H05 GATT inventory
keyConcepts.detail: Six services / 25 characteristics: 0x1800 Generic Access, 0x1801 Generic Attribute, Nordic Legacy DFU `00001530-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123` (H06 — unsigned-image-capable bootloader transport, 0x1531 control / 0x1532 packet / 0x1534 version), 0x180a Device Information (six chars), 0x180f Battery, and the 11-characteristic FightCamp custom service.

gotchas: THE BONDING REQUIREMENT HAS NO H-NUMBER AND IS NOT IN THE REPO. The single most important operational fact lives only in Kyle's memory file `C:/Users/kyler/.claude/projects/C--Users-kyler-punchlab/memory/project-tracker-duty-cycle.md`: the gloves must be PAIRED/BONDED with the tablet or EVERY link dies at ~37 s in every app. The glove sends an SMP Security Request ~4 s after each connection (authReq=0x01, Just Works); with no bond and nobody answering the OS consent prompt, Android's 30 s SMP timeout expires and the HOST terminates (GATT_CONN_TERMINATE_LOCAL_HOST, HCI reason 0x16). 4 s + 33 s ≈ 37.1 s. Pair once in Android Settings → Bluetooth → Pair new device; they advertise as "FightCam" (NOT "L Punch"/"R Punch", which are only `KNOWN_TRACKERS.displayName`). Verify with `adb shell dumpsys bluetooth_manager | grep -A3 "Bonded devices"`. Nothing in `src/ble/` initiates or checks a bond — `ConnectionState` has a 'bonding' member and `ConnectionBadge.tsx` renders it, but no code ever emits it. If the symptom returns (clean disconnects, no error, ~37 s lifetime, second glove failing fast with GATT 133), the bond was wiped — this is a manual OS step, not a code fix.

`ca281070` IS NOT DEVICE INFO. Proven on-wire 2026-08-29 (per the same memory file): it is the PENDING-RECORD COUNT, an LE uint16. The code still calls it `CHAR.DEVICE_INFO_READ` ('fixed device-info blob'), the init plan reads it with `label: 'read-deviceInfo-ca281070'` into `deviceInfo[uuid]`, and `trackerKeepalive.ts:186-193` logs its bytes per connect as 'glove device-info bytes' to 'compare firmware'. `docs/protocol/hypotheses.md` H12's next-test list still asks someone to go decode the 'device-info blob'. Nothing decodes it. A new session should treat the name as wrong and the value as a punch-backlog counter.

H07-REVISED IS CONTRADICTED BY SHIPPED CODE, INSIDE A SINGLE FILE. H07-REVISED in hypotheses.md still claims the tracker auto-streams on CCCD subscribe and that `buildInitializationPlan` 'can be an empty list'. That is false: `FightCampV1Commands.ts:65-74` says Hykso writes CLOCK_SYNC FIRST and 'without this write the tracker sits connected and idle and never emits punch frames', and the adapter does exactly that. Worse, the SAME CHAR object describes the SAME UUID twice with opposite conclusions — `LEGACY_COMMAND: 'ca281079-…'` (lines 47-50, 'H07-REVISED confirmed it is a no-op on current firmware') and `CLOCK_SYNC: 'ca281079-…'` (lines 65-74, required). Prefer CLOCK_SYNC; `LEGACY_COMMAND` is a legacy alias kept for old callers.

H08 ('Lenovo TB125FU blocks HCI snoop logging', status: confirmed, confidence: high) was later worked around but never updated. The memory file records btsnoop captures taken via `adb bugreport` → `FS/data/misc/bluetooth/logs/*.curf` after enabling the HCI snoop log in Developer options, with custom dissectors (`smp_probe.py`, `btsnoop_dissect.py`) written in a scratchpad. Every SMP/bonding and buffer-drain finding came from those captures. Do not conclude from H08 that snoop capture is impossible.

MIXED TIME BASES IN `CueMatcher.eventTimeMs`. For a non-recovered event it returns `event.receivedMonotonicTimeMs`, which is `performance.now()` (ms since the JS time origin, typically 1e4-1e7). For a `recovered` event it returns `event.trackerTimestampMs`, which is Unix epoch ms (~1.79e12). Those two values are then sorted together (`timed.sort((a,b) => a.atMs - b.atMs …)`), compared against `cue.windowStartMs`/`windowEndMs` under `gate: 'window'`, and subtracted from `scheduledMomentMs` to produce `offsetMs` — which is persisted to `cue_results.offset_ms`. Consequences: under `gate: 'window'` a recovered event is always outside the window (so always an extra, which happens to match intent); under `gate: 'open'` — the live path — it sorts LAST and can take a slot with an `offsetMs` of ~1.79e12. The decoder's comment at lines 156-163 claims `recovered` events are excluded from live matching, and `LiveCueMatcher.onPunchEvent` does skip them provisionally (line 233), but it still PUSHES them into `open.events` (line 209) so the authoritative settle pass DOES consider them.

THE 20 s KEEPALIVE WRITE IS THE BUFFER-DRAIN TRIGGER. `trackerKeepalive.ts` writes mode-normal (COMMAND1 = 0x01) every 20 s, and per the on-wire finding a mode-normal write is exactly what makes the tracker drain punches it buffered while disconnected. So backfilled records can arrive at any heartbeat tick mid-workout, not only on reconnect, and each one gets `recovered: true` if it is >3 s behind arrival. Hykso never sends Fetch Mode (3) — the drain rides mode-normal.

FIRMWARE VERSION IS NEVER ACTUALLY READ. `PunchStream` initializes `let state: ProtocolState = { connectionGeneration: 0 }` with no `firmwareVersion`, and nothing else in `src/` ever sets it (grep confirms only the adapter reads it and echoes it back). So `FightCampV1Adapter.decodeFrame` always falls through to `DEFAULT_FIRMWARE_MAJOR_VERSION = 4` and the 9-byte path is effectively hardcoded. `FightCampV1State.parseFirmwareMajor()` and `INITIAL_STATE` exist but have ZERO production callers — dead code. The init plan reads `ca281070`, not the 0x180a Software Revision String that H11 says carries the version. A v<4 tracker would be decoded as v>=4 and produce garbage flagged `malformed`.

DECODED PUNCH EVENTS ARE NOT PERSISTED DURING A PUNCHCRAFT WORKOUT. `PunchStream.onEventPersist` → `BleCaptureService.recordEvent` is wired in exactly ONE place: `src/app/(tabs)/velocity-lab/live.tsx:127`. The app-wide keepalive source (which every punchCraft workout attaches to) never passes it. Workout punches reach `punch_events` only at the end, via `persistWorkoutSession`, and only the subset that cue results actually NAME (`matchedEventsRef` in `_useWorkoutRunner.ts:1344` captures them from `recentEventsRef` as each cue settles, because by the bell they have aged out of the window). Unmatched punches and extras are never stored as events. Raw frames are unaffected — the facade's frame sink covers everything structurally.

`persistWorkoutSession` DROPS `velocityCalibrated`. The block at `src/storage/persistWorkoutSession.ts:141-170` passes `velocityRaw`, `accelerationRaw`, `velocityUnit` etc. but never `velocityCalibrated`, although `SessionRepository.appendPunchEvent` accepts it and the column exists. So `punch_events.velocity_calibrated` is NULL for every workout-persisted punch while the Velocity Lab capture path fills it. Note `cue_results.velocity_calibrated` IS written (via `toCueResultRows`), so the two tables disagree for the same punch.

THE TRANSMIT FLOOR MAKES 'missed' AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION (D13). The tracker does not transmit at all below some acceleration threshold — 10 deliberately soft uppercuts produced exactly 1 event, and the 'not a real punch' bytes 0 and 5 never appeared, so it is not classifying-then-rejecting. 'Did not throw' and 'threw too softly to exist' are the same absence of evidence. `toCueResultRows` writes `outcome: 'missed'` for both and neither may be shown as failure. Confidence is only medium (one set, and the blue tracker disconnected shortly after) — a repeat on a charged tracker is still owed.

`velocityCalibrated` IS NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS TYPE BYTES. The ×1.7 multiplier for `punchTypeRaw ∈ {1,2}` is retained purely for vendor arithmetic fidelity (so our number matches what the official app would have shown), NOT because 'power punch' is a confirmed reading — H12 removed that justification. Two frames with identical `velocityByteRaw` therefore differ by 1.7× depending on a byte nobody can interpret. Use `velocityRaw` for any cross-punch comparison.

HYPOTHESIS STATUS, SETTLED vs OPEN. SETTLED: H05 (GATT map, confirmed/high), H06 presence (confirmed/high — usability still proposed/medium), H08 (confirmed but worked around, see above), H11 byte layout (confirmed/high, from the decompiled APK), H12 (supported/high — the type byte is NOT a device-portable technique classifier; this is the load-bearing finding and it drives D12/D13). SUPPORTED: H01 (name + service UUID, high), H09 (Hykso hardware, high). SUPERSEDED: H07 by H07-REVISED and H11; H10 by H11; H11's punch-type reading by H12; H07-REVISED's 'no init write' by the clock-sync finding. STILL OPEN/WEAK: H02 (blue sleeps ~10 s, proposed/LOW — single session, never retested), H03 (LED encodes connection state, proposed/LOW), H04 (overlapping connects wedge the stack, proposed/MEDIUM — but `autoConnectTrackers` treats it as settled and connects strictly serially). There is no H13 or higher anywhere in the repo.

`docs/protocol/capture-index.md` IS EMPTY — 'Entries: (none yet — first rows appear after M01)'. `captures/` on disk is empty too. Only ONE fixture is committed (`spike-mt4wm1d8-fx6x.json`, 2026-08-23, red tracker only). The controlled-scenario list in `docs/protocol/README.md` (connect only, one left punch, five alternating, disconnect→punch→reconnect, sleep/wake, tracker A vs B) has never been systematically run and indexed, despite the README's own rule that every hypothesis needs ≥3 repetitions.

The protocol README's rules are stricter than current practice: 'Never send a write to a characteristic whose meaning has not been observed in official-app traffic.' The init plan writes `17` to COMMAND1 — a byte unnamed even in Hykso's own debug map — and that is justified by 'Hykso sends it every session', which satisfies the letter of the rule but not its spirit. Keep the rule in mind before adding any new write; the config characteristics 0x1074-0x1076 are explicitly meant to stay behind developer mode.

smells.concern: Returns epoch-ms for recovered events and performance.now()-ms for live ones, then sorts both in one comparator, window-tests them against monotonic bounds, and subtracts to produce the persisted `offsetMs`. This is the highest-value thing to review adversarially. A fix needs a decision about what clock the matcher works in, and whether recovered events should be filtered out of `open.events` entirely rather than half-excluded.

A recovered event is pushed into `open.events` and then skipped for provisional feedback. The settled pass therefore scores an event the live pass deliberately ignored, guaranteeing it appears in `corrections[]`. The decoder's own comment (FightCampV1Decoder.ts:156-163) asserts the opposite — that LiveCueMatcher 'excludes them from live matching while persistence still keeps them'. Either the comment or the code is wrong.

`profiles.find((p) => p.deviceAddress === deviceAddress)` is case-SENSITIVE and un-normalized, whereas `knownTrackers.ts` goes out of its way to compare addresses case-insensitively via `normalize()`. If ble-plx ever reports a lowercase MAC the form bonus silently stops firing — a failure that produces no error and no log, just the quiet absence of a reward.

Worth a design argument: migration 004 states that on this hardware 'which technique was thrown is unobservable and no code path may assert it', yet `typeConcordance` grants a visible gold affirmation derived from the device-local type byte, wired into `LiveMatch.affirmed`. The additive-only asymmetry is a thoughtful mitigation, but a false positive still rewards a wrong technique, and on blue the surviving `3 → uppercut` signal 'partly reflects motion size rather than technique' by its own notes. Both profiles are `provisional: true` from one athlete in one sitting; H12's own next-test (is the mapping stable across sessions?) has never run.

The `monitorCharacteristicForDevice` callback closes over `result`, which is declared with `const` AFTER the `manager.monitorCharacteristicForDevice(...)` call returns (line ~600). A callback that fired synchronously during registration would hit a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError inside the native notification path. Almost certainly safe with ble-plx's async delivery, but it is a latent ordering dependency in the hottest, least-recoverable code path in the app.

The dedup key is (device_address, tracker_timestamp_ms, punch_type_raw, velocity_raw) with timestamps quantized to 3.9 ms. Two genuinely distinct punches from one glove inside the same quantum with the same type and velocity bytes are indistinguishable and the second is silently dropped by INSERT OR IGNORE. The 18-byte two-record frame makes same-timestamp pairs plausible. More dangerous downstream: if a punch was already written by one path, a later `appendPunchEvent` with a DIFFERENT `id` is OR-IGNOREd, and the `cue_results.observed_event_id` FK naming that different id then fails and rolls back the entire session.

`parseFirmwareMajor` and `INITIAL_STATE` have no production callers; `ProtocolState.firmwareVersion` is never populated. The firmware-version plumbing is fully built and fully disconnected, so the 9-byte/13-byte switch is decided by a default constant. Either wire the 0x180a Software Revision read into the init plan and seed the state, or delete the legacy path and say so.

Two keys (`LEGACY_COMMAND`, `CLOCK_SYNC`) hold the identical UUID string with contradictory doc comments — one calling ca281079 a confirmed no-op, the other calling a write to it mandatory. `grep CHAR.LEGACY_COMMAND` to confirm nothing still uses the stale name, then collapse to one key.

The 20 s `setInterval` and the per-tracker `onConnectionChange` subscriptions are registered in `startTrackerKeepalive` but the connection-change unsubscribes are discarded (the returned `UnsubscribeFn` is dropped). `__resetTrackerKeepaliveForTests` clears the interval but not those listeners. In-app this is a process-lifetime singleton so it does not leak in practice, but a Metro reload re-registers them.

The `unknownType` quality flag can never be set. The condition is `decoded.punchType === 'unknown' && punchTypeRaw !== 0 && punchTypeRaw !== 5`, but `mapType()` unconditionally returns 'unknown', so the flag fires for every byte outside {0,5} — i.e. on essentially every real punch. Read the comment's intent (flag only when the raw enum was outside the KNOWN 0..5 set) against what the code does: it should probably be `punchTypeRaw > 5`. As written, `quality_flags` is noise on nearly every row.

keyConcepts.name: CALL_DISPATCH_LAG_MS = 71
keyConcepts.detail: Subtracted from every call's dispatch time. = 46.5 ms median scheduler lateness + 25.0 ms median play()→first-audio, measured on 46 release-build call bars. keyConcepts.name: TECHNIQUE_CALL_LEAD_MS = 250 / TECHNIQUE_LEADIN_LEAD_MS = 500 / NUMBERS_CALL_LEAD_MS = 100

keyConcepts.name: The set-aware breath formula
keyConcepts.detail: breathMs = max(MIN_BREATH_MS + DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS, min(dense, dense − BREATH_TRACK_GAIN · max(0, slotMs − BREATH_REF_SLOT_MS))) where slotMs is the bar's inter-punch interval (POSITIVE_INFINITY when the bar has <2 punches). BREATH_REF_SLOT_MS=300, BREATH_TRACK_GAIN=1.0, MIN_BREATH_MS=150, DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS=95 → effective floor 245 ms. Breath SHRINKS as the bar gets slower/wider, degenerating to the old constant on tight bars.

keyConcepts.name: Call duration budget

keyConcepts.name: Post-synthesis chain for a call clip
keyConcepts.detail: trimEnds(tailMs:120) → textureChain(PERSONA.texture, {profile:'single', finalAccentDb:0}) → ffmpeg -ar 48000 -ac 1 → UNCONDITIONAL rubberband tempo=1.35 formant=preserved (the 2026-09-11 persona-tempo-bump; click-scripts had been the only family shipping at 1.0× while everything else shipped at 1.35×) → conditional fit rubberband if still over window, capped at max(1.3, CALL_MAX_STRETCH[slot]).

keyConcepts.name: How a phrase is chosen and scheduled (click path — the live one)
keyConcepts.detail: Per round at work-entered: for each sequence cue, motif := tokens.map(punch ? `${n}${body?'b':''}` : '.').join('-'); slot := `call/${motif}`; clip := findClickScript(slot, roundSnapshottedVocabulary); callDispatchAtMs() places it to END breathMs before the bar's FIRST PUNCH (not bar start — a bar may open on a rest), minus CALL_DISPATCH_LAG_MS; giveUpAtMs = firstNodeMs + 500. Section 1 gets NO mid-round lead-in (pre-bell ceremony owns it); sections 2+ get `lead-in/<id>/r<N>s<M>` placed to END before the rep-0 CALL's dispatch (endByMs = rep0CallDispatchAtMs, falling back to scheduledStartMs). Calls whose window overlaps a lead-in's padded window (liStart = dispatchAtMs − 500) are dropped at BUILD time, except firstRep calls. At dispatch: voiceAllowed() gate, then audibleUntilMs() busy check — everything except firstRep retries until giveUpAtMs; firstRep dispatches on schedule because it owns its authored setupMeasures pad by construction (Variant B).

keyConcepts.name: playSequence APPENDS, never clears
keyConcepts.detail: If a sequence timer is active OR the queue is non-empty, new steps are PUSHED and the running timer walks the enlarged queue; only an idle lane seeds and starts. Fixes the 2026-08-31 TRF audio-doubling bug where a next cue's playPhrase clearSequence'd the previous cue's pending clips ('1-2' heard as '1, 1'). Double-timer races are prevented by construction: a new advanceSequence only starts when no timer is armed. cancel(belowPriority) still clears the sequence when any queued step is less urgent, and the LRU/one-shot cleanup is generation-guarded.

keyConcepts.name: AUDIO_PRIORITY
keyConcepts.detail: safety:0, bell:1, punchCommand:2, defenseFootwork:3, metric:4, coachingReminder:5. Lower cuts higher. cancel(belowPriority) drops only QUEUED items; a sounding clip is never chopped mid-syllable.

keyConcepts.name: PRODUCT — H12: the tracker cannot tell you which digit was thrown
keyConcepts.detail: Established 2026-08-23 by ~100-event controlled capture on both trackers, recorded as H12 in docs/protocol/hypotheses.md:259. The punch-type byte is not device-portable — the same technique yields a different byte per tracker. `TrackerPunchEvent.punchType` is therefore ALWAYS 'unknown'; only `punchTypeRaw` carries the byte. What the tracker gives reliably: hand (from slot assignment, not the payload), timing, and a velocity proxy. Consequence: matching is HAND-SEQUENCE only and the summary must say so, never claim technique accuracy. Second consequence: the tracker won't transmit below an acceleration floor, so soft technique punches produce no event at all — cue matching must distinguish 'dropped because soft' from 'missed the window'. TRUE and verified in the repo.

keyConcepts.detail: Dev tablet: Lenovo Android tablet (identified as TB125FU in the ceremony memory), supports wireless ADB (`adb pair <host>:<port>` then `adb connect`) as the DEFAULT connection method; USB is fallback. Trackers: blue = left `D7:34:B4:27:D5:84`, red = right `EA:69:2D:9C:FD:53`. Kyle wants blue=left/red=right treated as PERMANENT and hardcoded, never user-assigned. Trackers sleep aggressively — a firm tap wakes them before a scan will find them.

keyConcepts.name: BLE — THE root cause: trackers must be BONDED
keyConcepts.detail: Proven on the wire 2026-08-29. The glove sends an SMP Security Request ~4s after EVERY connection (`authReq=0x01` — bonding, no MITM, no SC: plain Just Works). With no bond and nobody answering the OS consent prompt, Android's 30s SMP timeout expires and the HOST terminates the link (`GATT_CONN_TERMINATE_LOCAL_HOST`, HCI reason 0x16): 4s + 33s ≈ the famous 37.1s 'cycle'. Fix: pair both gloves once in Android Settings → Bluetooth; they advertise as **"FightCam"** (not 'L Punch'/'R Punch' — those are our display names). Verify: `adb shell dumpsys bluetooth_manager | grep -A3 "Bonded devices"`. This CORRECTS the earlier belief that Hykso round-robins by design — its links die of the same timeout at 37.08s ± 45ms. Idle holds ARE native once bonded.

keyConcepts.name: BLE — random-static addresses: keep the scan, don't gate on it
keyConcepts.detail: Both trackers use random-static addresses (top two bits 0b11). rxandroidble resolves address strings via `BluetoothAdapter.getRemoteDevice(String)` which assumes PUBLIC, so a scan (or a bond) is what teaches the stack the true type — removing the scan from the connect path (tried 2026-08-29) broke connecting outright. BUT do NOT gate connecting on the scan: a bonded glove may advertise DIRECTED at its partner and never appear in a general scan while being instantly connectable, so an unseen known tracker still gets a direct attempt.

keyConcepts.name: BLE — ble-plx error semantics on Android
keyConcepts.detail: A connect TIMEOUT is reported as **"Operation was cancelled" (errorCode 2)** because its `doFinally` fires `cancelled()` before the real timeout surfaces — this is NOT evidence of external cancellation; compare `durationMs` against the timeout. `errorCode 203` ('already connected') means OUR OWN orphaned link survived a Metro reload — ADOPT it, never treat it as a failure (doing so caused an endless connect/cancel loop). `ble.connect.failed` logs errorCode/attErrorCode/androidErrorCode/durationMs.

keyConcepts.name: BLE — punch buffering and the pending-record count
keyConcepts.detail: A tracker BUFFERS punches thrown while disconnected and drains them on the next mode-normal write (COMMAND1=1). Hykso never sends 'Fetch Mode'/3. `ca281070` is the PENDING-RECORD COUNT (LE uint16), not device info. Each record carries an absolute epoch timestamp (3.9 ms quantization) — which is why clock-sync is written first on every connect. Records arriving 22–66s late were recovered on-wire. The decoder marks such records `recovered: true` (>3s behind arrival) so `LiveCueMatcher` excludes them from live scoring while persistence keeps them.

keyConcepts.name: BLE — connection hygiene rules that cost nights
keyConcepts.detail: (1) ConnectionPriority.High on BOTH links makes this tablet's scheduler shed the newer link ('the second glove always dies') — stay **Balanced**; High only ever briefly during one glove's init. (2) NEVER evict a slot in a bring-up state (connecting/initializing/recovering) when the native stack confirms the link (THIS_SESSION_STATES in autoConnectTrackers). (3) App-wide keepalive lives at `src/protocol/trackerKeepalive.ts` — punch streams start at connect, heartbeat writes mode-normal + reads battery (0x180F/0x2A19). (4) Never remove the `ble.device.disconnected` log — silence there cost a night. (5) The Hykso app installed on the tablet WILL fight punchCraft for gloves: force-stop `com.hykso.hyksofit` before tracker work. (6) `dumpsys` MAC 'presence' includes cached entries, not live links.

keyConcepts.name: BLE — PC-direct glove spike #387 verdict (newest hardware finding)
keyConcepts.detail: Complete 2026-09-27, M45-08: **GO on feasibility, adopt for ARCHITECTURE not latency.** From the PC via bleak 3.0.2/WinRT, `BleakClient(pair=True)` is MANDATORY and must pair BEFORE service discovery (post-connect pairing is too late — the ~4s SMP request stalls WinRT discovery to timeout). 20s keepalive; dual-glove 5 min, 62+26 live punches, 0 malformed, 0 disconnects, 1–2s bonded reconnects. THE LATENCY PREMISE DIED ON ITS OWN DATA: PC-direct removes only the WS hop (5–14 ms of ~170 ms, <10%) while all the jitter (56–92 ms median above floor) is upstream of the split. Harness: `tools/spikes/pc-ble/` (scan.py, spike.py; commits `9d53f0e7`, `8b7e79a2`). MEASUREMENT TRAP: `arrival − tracker_timestamp` is inflated by the clock-sync write delay, per-glove (two gloves on one radio differed 50 ms in FLOOR) — only jitter-above-floor is trustworthy. HARDWARE: this PC's onboard RZ616 has NO ANTENNAS (max RSSI −92 dBm, ~1 m bubble); a USB BT dongle gave 28 devices/−54 dBm. Bonds are PER-ADAPTER on Windows. Only open box: tablet bond-coexistence.

keyConcepts.name: HARDWARE — ADB tap coordinate frame (identity transform)
keyConcepts.detail: Proven 2026-08-30 after ~30 min of rotation-math dead ends: `adb shell wm size` prints `1200x2000` (natural portrait) but the app runs landscape so `screencap` returns 2000x1200, and `adb shell input tap X Y` uses the CURRENT landscape frame — screencap X ≈ tap X, screencap Y ≈ tap Y, NO rotation transform. `dumpsys display | grep mCurrentOrientation` reads 3; do NOT translate against it. Authoritative source for coords: `uiautomator dump /sdcard/ui.xml` — `bounds="[x1,y1][x2,y2]"` is in the same frame; tap the box center. Pull the dump with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` prefixed or Git Bash mangles `/sdcard/...`. Some RN handlers ignore instantaneous taps — `adb shell input swipe X Y X Y 120` (a 120 ms press-release) gets through when a bare tap doesn't.

keyConcepts.name: HARDWARE — on-device SQLite inspection (four traps)
keyConcepts.detail: (1) expo-sqlite stores in `files/SQLite/`, NOT `databases/` — an empty `databases/` is the wrong path, not a missing DB; confirm with `run-as com.kyleruff.punchcraft find . -name "*.db*"`. (2) There is NO `sqlite3` binary on the tablet — pull and inspect locally (Python stdlib sqlite3, or Node's `node:sqlite`). (3) PULL WITH BASH, never PowerShell: PowerShell's `>` is text-encoding and silently corrupts binary ('file is not a database'). Use `adb exec-out run-as com.kyleruff.punchcraft cat files/SQLite/punchcraft.db > local.db` and sanity-check `head -c 16 local.db | xxd` = 'SQLite format 3'. Pull all three of .db, -wal, -shm (WAL is on; the main file alone looks stale). (4) `adb push` from Git Bash mangles the REMOTE path — do PUSHES from PowerShell, PULLS from bash. keyConcepts.name: VOICE — the echo root cause and the single-texture DOCTRINE
keyConcepts.detail: Kyle 2026-09-02: 'echoey and lo-fi'. keyConcepts.name: AUDIO — the 48 kHz playlist law (dead-air root cause)
keyConcepts.detail: Dead air at `createAudioPlaylist` track boundaries is a SAMPLE-RATE RENEGOTIATION, not a clip problem: 24k→24k and 48k→48k cost ~0; 48k→24k ≈ +95 ms; 24k→48k ≈ +193 ms — about 800 ms across a seven-track walkout. Silence tracks (18) and theme clips (21) were 24 kHz while intro/warn/rec clips are 48 kHz. Fixed by regenerating/resampling 39 files at 48 kHz (+5.5 MB), NOT by normalising the whole corpus (+241 MB for assets that never sit in a playlist). `SHIPPED_SAMPLE_RATE = 48000` and `OUT_SAMPLE_RATE` in tools/voice/persona.mjs are the ONE rate reader — any renderer whose output can sit in a playlist must use it, never a literal. keyConcepts.name: VOICE — body shots are HYPHENATED "One-bee", never fused and never spaced

The hyphen is not stylistic — it is the only input format Chatterbox reliably fuses. Implemented in `spokenFor()` in tools/voice/prosody.mjs; any override in tools/voice/overrides.json must keep the hyphen. Start from the hyphenated text for ANY future letter-number fusion in this engine. ASYMMETRY TO KEEP: techniques vocab uses 'Body jab'/'Body cross' and does NOT fuse, because techniques front-load the target so the utterance is predictive from word 1, while numbers put the target-changing suffix LAST. keyConcepts.name: TIMING — token-order forensics: three independent root causes (all fixed in a0e3f3b)
keyConcepts.detail: (1) CATCH-UP BURST STROBE (the core one): the runner's token-due handler called `syncFromEngine()` + `pushStore(true)` PER EVENT; when the 50 ms interval stalls, `CueEngine.fireDueTokens` publishes every overdue token inside ONE `engine.tick(...)` (measured 74 events across 63 distinct workElapsedMs values, worst tick firing FIVE tokens), so the row strobed through history in ~1 ms and the avatar followed in lockstep. Fix: advance the monotonic cursor only; render once in the tick loop. **Do NOT 'fix' this in CueEngine — its tick-size-invariance contract is pinned by 60 seeded-timeline tests and is correct.** (2) MATCHER ORPHANED after the round's first cue: acceptance windows overlap by `DEFAULT_GRACE_BEFORE_MS` (200 ms) so `cue-window-opened(N)` arrives BEFORE `cue-window-closed(P)`; LiveCueMatcher's single unkeyed `open` slot let N discard P, then P's close consumed N, and every later punch became `extra`. Fix: key open/close/cancel by cue id. (3) AVATAR PINNED EXTENDED: `punchAvatarManifest` maps step1 → `-s2.png` = STRIKE and step2 → guard (deliberate, despite PunchAvatarCard's header comment saying the reverse); the `holdingGuard` branch returned step1. keyConcepts.name: TOOLING — backlog seeding operational traps
keyConcepts.detail: From a real 48-issue seed 2026-08-23. (1) PRE-FLIGHT IS MANDATORY AFTER A RENAME: seed.mjs matches by EXACT TITLE, so a stale GitHub title silently creates a DUPLICATE — diff JSON titles against GitHub for epics, milestones and `area:*` labels first (the fixes here were `gh issue edit 5 --title ...` and `gh label edit area:punchlab --name area:punchcraft`; a label rename propagates in place). (2) THE PROJECT PHASE IS O(all issues) AND LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A FREEZE: `assignToProject` re-sets all four single-selects for every issue each run (200 issues × 4 gh spawns ≈ 800 processes) — 10+ minutes with NO log output and near-zero parent CPU because Node blocks in spawnSync. Do not diagnose it as a hang. Poll `gh project item-list --format json` instead. (3) FASTER PATH: batch all four fields into ONE aliased GraphQL mutation per item (20 items in ~1 min vs ~4 CLI calls each). (4) `Sub-issue link failed for <KEY>: {}` is COSMETIC — already-linked issues return an empty error body the classifier can't match. (5) Foreground Bash caps at 10 minutes — background long seeds or they get SIGTERM'd (exit 143); the script is idempotent so a killed run resumes. (6) Inside `node -e` on Windows, `/tmp/x` resolves to `C:\tmp\x` and `/c/Users/...` fails to require — use `C:/Users/...`.

workout.summary: The workout model is a 3-layer pure-TypeScript stack under `src/domain/workout/`: (1) contracts + combo notation in `WorkoutTokens.ts` (WorkoutToken / WorkoutBlock / ProgramRound, `parseCombo`/`formatCombo`), (2) content — a 60-combo / 18-ladder authored corpus (`corpus/comboCorpusV1.ts`) plus a legacy 32-motif library (`comboLibrary.ts`) plus 22 hand-authored "click map" workouts (`samples/clickMaps.ts` + `samples/quickWorkouts.ts`), and (3) the generator `generateWorkout(recipe)` → `roundFill.fillScoredRound`, which fills every scored round to the bell on a 7-phase build-up template (D26). Two parallel content paths ship simultaneously: picking a library workout runs a click map (hand-authored bars, rendered coach clips per slot); picking nothing runs the seeded generator from the corpus. Everything downstream (`programs/CueTimeline.ts` → `programs/RhythmMap.ts` → the runner) consumes `ProgramRound[]`, so blocks/tokens are the real contract boundary. The whole thing is deeply boxing-specific at the *type* level — `PunchNumber = 1|2|3|4|5|6`, stance-relative lead/rear semantics, four technique families, `'left'|'right'` glove resolution, boxing-worded defense/footwork/coach enums — and there is no discipline/activity-type abstraction anywhere in the repo, so a non-boxing workout type cannot be expressed in the current model without either widening `WorkoutToken` or introducing a token-vocabulary indirection. Last commit 2026-09-26; generator is at `GENERATOR_VERSION = '1.2.0'`.

keyConcepts.name: Combo notation (D10) — parse/format asymmetry
keyConcepts.detail: Segments split on '-'. A punch is `/^(\d+)(b?)$/i` with the number 1..6 (lowercase `b` on serialize, uppercase B badge on screen). `.` is a REST slot. Commands use SPACED spellings in notation, not the hyphenated enum values: 'bob and weave'→'bob-weave', 'step off'→'step-off', 'cut off the ring'→'cut-off-ring', 'double up', "put it on em", 'touch and go'. `formatCombo` DROPS rest tokens, so the round-trip law `formatCombo(parseCombo(s)) === s` holds only for rest-free notation — padded '1-.-2-.' formats back to '1-2'. ComboParseError codes: 'empty'|'unknown-segment'|'punch-out-of-range'|'malformed-punch'. parseCombo emits placeholder beatOffsets 0,1,2,… — authored `offsets` overwrite them in layBlocks.

keyConcepts.name: The two content libraries (and which one runs)
keyConcepts.detail: (a) `MOTIFS` in comboLibrary.ts — 32 entries, ids m-*, fields {id,notation,role:'combo'|'defense'|'footwork',punches,length,complexity 1-5,hasBody,offsets?,defense?,footwork?}. Used today ONLY for defense/footwork counters and the no-ladder fallback. (b) the corpus: 60 combos (20 per tier) + 18 BUILD_UP_SETS (4-5 stages each, 6 per tier), consumed by roundFill via BUILD_UP_SETS. CORPUS_MOTIFS is built but the generator does not select from it. 'combo' role motifs from MOTIFS are never chosen when a ladder survives.

keyConcepts.name: motifsFor() hard filter
keyConcepts.detail: A motif survives only if: role in query.roles; `length <= min(query.maxLength, recipe.maximumComboPunches)`; `complexity <= min(query.complexityCeiling ?? 5, recipe.comboComplexity)`; not (hasBody && bodyShotPercent<=0); every punch in `recipe.enabledPunches`; for defense/footwork, frequency !== 'off' AND the command is enabled.

keyConcepts.name: generateWorkout(recipe, options) pipeline
keyConcepts.detail: 1. `buildRoundSchedule(recipe.durationMinutes)`. 2. `bpm = CADENCE_PROFILES[recipe.cadenceProfile].nominalBpm` (NOT bpmForRecipe). 3. `rng = makeRng(`${recipe.seed}|${recipe.generatorVersion}`)`. 4. equal-weight shells → `allocateRoundTargets(totalPunchGoal, shells, focus)`. 5. per entry: aux round via `buildAuxRound` or `fillScoredRound(order, target, p, entry, recipe, bpm, rng, options)` where `p = scoredIndex/(scoredCount-1)`. 6. tally distribution (a block's punches spread evenly across its distinct punch tokens). 7. warnings: fallback rounds, uncovered rounds (coverageAudit), >15% goal drift. Options: `{voiceReady?(notation):boolean, setupCallouts?:{reserveMsFor}}` — both default off/true.

keyConcepts.name: The 7-phase build-up round (D26) and PHASE_SHARE
keyConcepts.detail: `PHASE_SHARE = {base:0.17, build1:0.17, volume:0.11, build2:0.17, bodyVariation:0.14, movement:0.1, pressure:0.14}`. Each repeat phase solves its gap so the block spans its TIME budget: `reps = clamp(round(desiredPunches/pick.punchCount), 2, 12)`, `gapBeats = clamp(budgetBeats/reps - comboBeats, MIN_GAP_BEATS, 5) * tighten`, then `fitReps = clamp(floor(budgetBeats/(comboBeats+gapBeats)), 2, 12)` — time wins over punch share. `effTarget = round(target * 0.88)`; pressure phase uses tighten=0.7 and `shiftCadence(+1)`.

keyConcepts.name: Escalation curves
keyConcepts.detail: `complexityCeilingAt(p) = 2 + round(p*3)`; `lengthCeilingAt(p) = 2 + round(p*3)`; `gapBeatsAt(p) = max(0.75, 1.4 - p*0.5)`; ladder `maxLen = min(recipe.maximumComboPunches, lengthCeilingAt(p)+2)`; `wantedRank = min(recipeRank, round(p*recipeRank))` with TIER_RANK {beginner:0,intermediate:1,advanced:2}. Ladder weight = (4 if rank===wantedRank else 2 if lower else 1) × (1+3×jabShare) × (1+2×leadShare|rearShare for bias lead|rear).

keyConcepts.name: callsPerRound frequency bands
keyConcepts.detail: off→0, light→2+int(2) (2-3), moderate→5+int(4) (5-8), heavy→9+int(6) (9-14). BUT phase 6 caps them: `defenseLeft = min(2, callsPerRound(defenseFrequency))` and `footworkLeft = min(1, callsPerRound(footworkFrequency))`, plus a `guard++ < 8` loop bound.

keyConcepts.name: Coverage repair (D26)
keyConcepts.detail: REPAIR_BELL_MARGIN_MS=2_000, MAX_REPAIR_PASSES=24: appends 2-rep copies of the highest-jab-share ladder stage (gap × 0.8) while `workMs - span > 2000`, then up to 6 single-rep top-offs. Audited by `coverageAudit(blocks, workDurationMs, COVERAGE_EPSILON_MS=5000)`.

keyConcepts.name: Mandatory same-move ceremony
keyConcepts.detail: Any contiguous run of one notation longer than `MANDATORY_SAME_MOVE_MS = 60_000` must be announced. Pattern choice: all-jab → 'co-jab-volume'; `/^(1b?|2b?|1-2|2-1)$/` → 'co-power-coast'; else 'co-coast'. If the reservation pushes the span past the bell, trailing repair reps are `pop()`ed to pay for it. Only runs when `opts.setupCallouts` is injected.

keyConcepts.name: layBlocks — the one lowering function
keyConcepts.detail: `layBlocks(specs, bpm)`: cursor += beatsToMs(spec.leadInBeats ?? 0, bpm) (the ceremony reservation = empty laid time BEFORE the block); tokens = withOffsets(parseCombo(notation), offsets) (throws if offsets.length !== tokens.length); `durationMs = durationBeats !== undefined ? beatsToMs(durationBeats,bpm) : blockDurationMs(tokens, gapBeats, bpm) * repeat`; cursor += durationMs. `blockDurationMs = beatsToMs(maxBeatOffset + gapBeats, bpm)`.

keyConcepts.name: blockPunchCount precedence
keyConcepts.detail: `block.targetPunches` (if set) wins; otherwise `punchTokenCount × (repeat ?? 1)`. `roundPunchCount` sums it. Under D26 `ProgramRound.targetPunches` is DERIVED from the laid blocks, never asserted — the recipe goal is directional only.

keyConcepts.name: Round schedule constants
keyConcepts.detail: ROUND_WORK_MS = 240_000 (4:00, D21 superseded §9's 3:00); REST_MS = 60_000; COOLDOWN_MS = 60_000; WARM_UP_MS = 120_000 (dead — every SHAPES entry has `warmUp: false`). SHAPES: 20→4 rounds, 30→6, 40→8, 60→12. Final round has `restAfterMs: 0`. `activeSeconds = rounds × 240` (scored rounds only). Deliberately NO override parameters.

keyConcepts.name: Click map format (what the shipped library workouts actually are)
keyConcepts.detail: `ClickRow {motif, rate: 1|1.5|2, reps, leadIn, setupMeasures?}`; `ClickRound {theme, rows, stance?, rest?}`; `ClickMap {bpm, rounds}`. A measure = 4 beats; `measuresPerRep(slots,rate)`: 8 slots → 3 (rate 1) / 1.5 (rate 2); 4 slots → 2 (rate 1) / 1 (rate 1.5 or 2). `breathBeats = measuresPerRep*4 - slots/rate`. `clickSpecs` lowers each row to ONE 'repeated-combo' BlockSpec with `gapBeats = breathBeats + 1/rate` and `leadInBeats = setupMeasures*4`. Budget: every round's row measures + setup gaps must equal `bpm` EXACTLY. SETUP_GAP_MEASURES = 2. 22 maps total, 164 rows in CLICK_MAPS.

keyConcepts.name: Voice gate wiring (the generator's content ceiling)
keyConcepts.detail: live.tsx passes `voiceReady: (n) => findComboAnnounce(n, vocabulary) !== undefined` where vocabulary = recipe.voiceVocabulary==='names' ? 'techniques' : 'numbers'. The manifest holds 109 distinct combinations × 2 vocabularies. Verified: all 60 corpus combos, all 54 multi-token ladder stages and all 32 MOTIFS notations have clips in BOTH vocabularies, so `voiceReady` currently rejects nothing. Adding ANY new notation to the corpus/library requires re-running `tools/voice/make-combo-announce-clips.mjs` or the ladder silently drops out of selection.

keyConcepts.name: Strike catalog derivations (all pure functions of the token)
keyConcepts.detail: familyFor: 1→jab, 2→cross, 3|4→hook, 5|6→uppercut. handFor: odd→'lead', even→'rear'. nodeIdFor: `node.${n}` / `node.${n}b` — 12 unique nodes, head and body are DIFFERENT nodes. TECHNIQUE_FULL {1 Jab, 2 Cross, 3 Lead hook, 4 Rear hook, 5 Lead uppercut, 6 Rear uppercut}; TECHNIQUE_COMPACT {3 Hook, 5 Lead upper, 6 Rear upper}; NUMBER_WORD One..Six; body numberCall is `${word}-bee`.
