Only GR03 is actually honoured (verbatim library emission + `bodyVariationOf` approved transformation).

keyConcepts.name: CueTimeline block-kind routing (the consumer contract)
keyConcepts.detail: SEQUENCE_KINDS = {exact-combo, repeated-combo, defense-counter, footwork-exit} → one CueInstance per repeat. COUNT_SCORED_KINDS = {volume-burst, open-pressure, coast, active-recovery} → ONE cue with `scoring:'count'` and empty expectedPunches. Anything else lands in `RoundTimeline.deferredBlockIds` — i.e. a 'sustained-strike' block is silently dropped from the timeline. Note goalAllocation.ts has its OWN, different COUNT_SCORED_KINDS = {volume-burst, open-pressure, coast} (no active-recovery).

gotchas: BOXING IS BAKED IN AT THE TYPE LEVEL — there is no discipline/activity-type/modality concept anywhere in the repo (grepped src, docs, tools: zero hits). To add a non-boxing workout type you must touch, at minimum: `PunchNumber = 1|2|3|4|5|6` and the 1..6 range check in parseCombo (WorkoutTokens.ts:25,254); `Stance`/`BlockStance` (WorkoutTokens.ts:28,34); the three command enums and their notation word-maps (WorkoutTokens.ts:36-38, 211-240); `STRIKE_CATALOG` + familyFor/handFor/nodeIdFor/TECHNIQUE_FULL/TECHNIQUE_COMPACT/NUMBER_WORD (strikeCatalog.ts:99-160); `LEAD_NUMBERS={1,3,5}` + resolveHand (StanceMapper.ts:39-58); `IMPLIED_TYPE` (CueTimeline.ts:209-216); `PUNCH_NAMES` (recipeSummary.ts:30-37); `PUNCHES`/`DEFENSE`/`FOOTWORK` label tables (EnablementMenu.tsx:44-60); `punchAvatarKey` + punchAvatarManifest (12 asset pairs); `TECHNIQUE_WORDS`/`MOVEMENT_WORDS`/`NUMBER_WORDS` in tools/voice/prosody.mjs:30-64.

BOXING ASSUMPTIONS HIDDEN INSIDE THE GENERATOR (not just in types): roundFill weights ladders by jab share `1 + 3*shares.jab` (line ~368) and by lead/rear parity `n % 2` (line ~348); the repair pass sorts candidates by `jabShareOf` (line ~601); `allJab` detection `t.replace('b','') === '1'` (lines 463-464, 680); the power-coast regex `/^(1b?|2b?|1-2|2-1)$/` (line ~688); `bodyVariationOf` scans `/^[1-6]$/` and appends 'b' (line ~252); `buildAuxRound` uses `recipe.enabledPunches[0] ?? 1` as 'the jab' (generateWorkout.ts:48). setupCallouts.familyPatternFor hardcodes 1/2=straights, 3/4=hooks, 5/6=uppercuts and 'square' = {1,2,3,4} (setupCallouts.ts:168-186).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY GENERIC AND REUSABLE AS-IS: cadence.ts (beats↔ms, blockDurationMs), roundSchedule.ts (interval timer shapes), goalAllocation.ts (largest-remainder count split; only the kind names are domain-specific), seededRandom.ts, samples/authoring.ts layBlocks/blockPunchCount/blocksSpanMs, GeneratedWorkout.validateGeneratedWorkout (except the `kind==='round'` ↔ countsTowardGoal rule), mapValidation.ts coverage/silence audits, planMutation.ts, clickMaps.ts measure arithmetic (measuresPerRep/breathBeats/rowMeasures), chunks.ts + composeFromChunks.ts (chunk linking is vocabulary-agnostic except the motif notation). The cleanest seam for a non-boxing type is the `WorkoutToken`/notation vocabulary plus a pluggable token→(spoken label, node id, hand) resolver; everything above the token is already generic.

FIVE WorkoutRecipe FIELDS ARE DECLARED BUT READ NOWHERE outside WorkoutRecipe.ts: `velocityZoneEmphasis`, `cueRhythmProfile`, `metricAnnouncementFrequency`, `commandVocabularyStyle`, `visualLeadTimeMs`. Five of the seven 'D14 advanced controls' are therefore inert. Do not assume setting them changes anything.

`recipe.stanceMode` NEVER reaches the generator. roundFill/generateWorkout read only bias, bodyShotPercent, defense/footworkFrequency, enabledDefense/Footwork, enabledPunches, maximumComboPunches, cadenceProfile, comboComplexity (via tierFor), focus, durationMinutes, totalPunchGoal, seed, generatorVersion. Every generated block gets `stance: 'inherit'` (layBlocks default), so switch-by-round only exists in the hand-authored `switchByRound` sample. `bias: 'left'|'right'` is also in the type but roundFill only weights 'lead' and 'rear'.

generateWorkout uses `CADENCE_PROFILES[recipe.cadenceProfile].nominalBpm` directly (generateWorkout.ts:122) while the runner expands and plays at `bpmForRecipe(workout.recipe)` (_useWorkoutRunner.ts:434). These agree only while `metronome.enabled === false`. Generate a recipe with `metronome.enabled: true` or `globalSpeed !== 1` and the blocks were LAID at one BPM but re-expanded at another: startOffsetMs stays fixed in ms while intra-block beat math scales, so blocks overrun/underfill. The hand-authored samples work around this by choosing coachTempo so `bpmForRecipe === MAP.bpm`.

THE SHIPPED LIBRARY WORKOUTS DO NOT USE THE GENERATOR. All 22 samples (`samples/index.ts`) are built from CLICK_MAPS / chunk compositions and emit only 'repeated-combo' blocks. generateWorkout runs only when the athlete picks no sample (live.tsx:301). So changes to roundFill affect nothing the user normally sees, and changes to clickMaps affect nothing the generator produces.

39 of 164 click-map rows have a spoken `leadIn` whose bar count disagrees with `reps` — always the lead-in claiming ~2 more bars, e.g. `{motif:'1-2-1-.', rate:2, reps:16, leadIn:'…double-time, eighteen bars…'}` and `{motif:'1-1-2-.', rate:2, reps:38, leadIn:'…forty bars…'}` in clickMaps.ts. Traceable to the 2026-09-04 'fit-round-openers / opener-pad rebalance' that trimmed reps to pay for setup pads without re-authoring the copy. `clickMapsSelfCheck` validates the measure budget, digit-free copy, rest scripts and pace caps — but NOT the bar count. The wrong numbers are already baked into the rendered wavs (verified: 262/262 lead-in slots match the manifest text exactly, 0 drift), so fixing either side forces a voice re-render.

`clickScriptManifest` clips are looked up by SLOT (`lead-in/<workout>/rNsM`), never by text. Nothing in the test suite asserts `row.leadIn === clip.text`. Editing a `leadIn` string therefore keeps playing the OLD audio with no failure anywhere; the invariant holds today only because the render tool reads clickMaps.ts.

`clickMapsSelfCheck` requires every round's `sum(rowMeasures) + sum(setupMeasures)` to equal `bpm` EXACTLY (a 4:00 round at B bpm holds exactly B measures). Any edit to a motif's slot count, rate or reps breaks a denominator, and `compose()` in composeFromChunks.ts THROWS AT MODULE LOAD on a mis-filled quick workout — i.e. the whole app bundle fails to import, not just a test.

Chunk identity includes the exact rep count: `chunkSignature = `${motif}|@${rate}|x${reps}|${stance ?? '-'}``. Tuning reps on a chunk creates a NEW chunk (`jab-cross-hook-cross-x18` vs `-x15` vs `-x13`), and `chunksSelfCheck` forbids two chunks with the same signature.

`gapBeats` in clickSpecs is `breathBeats + 1/rate`, NOT just the breath — the laid rep span is measured to the LAST PUNCH'S ONSET, so the gap must carry the final slot's own width. Getting this wrong under-filled rounds ~12% and left ~30s of dead air before the bell (caught 2026-09-02, comment at clickMaps.ts:128-131).

The generator uses TWO independent RNG streams: the main `makeRng(`${seed}|${generatorVersion}`)` and a per-round callout stream `makeRng(`${seed}|${GENERATOR_VERSION}|callouts|r${order}`)`. `pickCallout` always draws even when it will skip, to keep the draw count stable across clip availability. CALL ORDER IS THE DETERMINISM CONTRACT — inserting an rng call anywhere in roundFill changes every generated workout and requires bumping GENERATOR_VERSION (currently '1.2.0').

`parseCombo` on a defense/footwork notation like `'1-step-off-2'` is IMPOSSIBLE — '-' is the segment separator, so the SPACED spelling ('step off', 'bob and weave', 'cut off the ring') is authoritative in notation. `normalizeWord` strips apostrophes and collapses whitespace, so "put it on 'em" and 'put it on em' both parse.

Corpus tokens are stored UPPERCASE-B (`["1","2B"]`) but every clip key and every `formatCombo` output is lowercase-b. Always go through `canonicalNotation(tokens)` (corpusMotifs.ts:62) — a raw `tokens.join('-')` gives '1-2B' and misses the clip.

`GeneratedWorkout.roundPunchTargets` must have exactly one entry per SCORED round (the validator enforces length), but `ProgramRound.targetPunches` on each round is the DERIVED realized count, so the two arrays disagree by design under D26. `allocateRoundTargets` is called against empty shells before any block exists, so it falls back to `workDurationMs` weighting (equal rounds → equal split).

The cooldown round is NOT covered to the bell: `buildAuxRound` emits a single 20-beat active-recovery block, measured at 12000 ms of a 60000 ms window. Coverage repair applies only to scored rounds. The warm-up branch of `buildAuxRound` is unreachable because every SHAPES entry sets `warmUp: false` (D21 removed the 30-minute warm-up).

`generateWorkout`'s own header claims it reuses 'the high-goal density rule (`assessDensity`)' — it does not. `assessDensity` is referenced only from goalAllocation.ts and its test. Other declared-but-unused exports: `BEATS_PER_BURST_PUNCH`, `roundSpanMs`, `SETUP_ROUND_OPEN_EXTRA_MS`, `familyPatternFor`, `coastFor`/`COAST_DURATIONS`, `GENERATOR_RULES`, `COMBOS_BY_ID`, `getCombosByTier`, `OPTIONAL_FOOTWORK_WRAPPERS`, `withSustainedStrike` (fixture-only), `padBlocksToRound` (fixture-only).

corpusMotifs.ts's header says the corpus motifs are 'NOT merged into MOTIFS yet' and that the generator 'keeps selecting from the legacy 31'. Both statements are stale: MOTIFS has 32 entries, and roundFill already selects corpus ladders (BUILD_UP_SETS) as the round spine — MOTIFS is now only defense/footwork + fallback.

Stop reading `CLICK_MAPS` directly — `allClickMaps()` (CLICK_MAPS + QUICK_CLICK_MAPS, 22 maps) is the view every gate and render tool must iterate. The header of allClickMaps.ts records three tools that previously walked only the literal maps and therefore never fit-checked or rendered a composed workout's motifs.

smells.concern: The module header says 'pressure repetition … the final round flurries instead', but on the last round the code pushes the `open-pressure` flurry AND THEN calls `addRepeatPhase(completed, …)`. Verified on glass-equivalent output: gen-r3 runs `open-pressure 1-2 (tp40) @187s` then `1-2-3b-3-2 ×9 @207s`, so the final round ends on the pressure pattern, not the flurry. Either the comment or the ordering is wrong.

PHASE_SHARE budgets the movement phase at 0.10 (24s of a 240s round) but phase 6 is capped at `min(2, …)` defense + `min(1, …)` footwork blocks, which span ~5s in practice. ~19s per round of the movement budget silently falls through to the repair pass, which pads the base pattern instead. The template's stated proportions do not describe what it produces.

Ladder selection has no cross-round memory. With defaultRecipe() rounds 2 and 4 both draw 'Body-Head Hook Double' and produce byte-identical content for their first nine blocks. Doc §16 asks for one theme per round and 'no more than two materially new motifs in one round'; nothing prevents the same ladder being drawn repeatedly, and `ProgramRound.theme` is just the ladder name so the duplicate is visible to the athlete.

The coverage-repair tail is crude: round 1 of the default workout ends with nine consecutive `1-1 ×2` blocks (~21.6s of the same two punches), round 3 with ten `1-2 ×2`. It sits just under MANDATORY_SAME_MOVE_MS (60s) so no ceremony fires, and `blockCount -= 1` / `blockCount += 0` id-reclaim bookkeeping around the probe specs is fragile enough that a future edit will mint duplicate block ids.

`const bpm = CADENCE_PROFILES[recipe.cadenceProfile].nominalBpm` bypasses `bpmForRecipe(recipe)`, which is the documented bridge and what the runner uses. Generation and playback silently diverge the moment `metronome.enabled` or `globalSpeed` is set on a generated recipe. This is also why the cadence.ts header's 'byte-identical' claim only holds for the sample path.

Two independent, divergent COUNT_SCORED_KINDS sets (CueTimeline includes 'active-recovery', goalAllocation does not) and a THIRD routing decision via SEQUENCE_KINDS. 'sustained-strike' is in no set at all, so such a block is dropped into `deferredBlockIds` with no error. Block-kind semantics should live beside the BlockKind union, not be re-derived per consumer.

BlockKind carries 10 values of which 'exact-combo' is emitted by nothing, 'coast' is emitted by nothing (its whole support module coast.ts is dead), and 'sustained-strike' exists only in a retired `__fixtures__` file. Three of ten kinds are speculative, and each one forces every consumer to handle a case that cannot occur.

The spoken bar count in `leadIn` disagrees with `reps` in 39 of 164 rows, and the disagreement is already rendered into the shipped wavs. The self-check lints digits, empty copy, rest scripts and pace ceilings but not the one number the athlete can verify by counting. A `leadIn`-vs-`reps` and `leadIn`-vs-`clip.text` assertion are both cheap and currently absent.

Five inert fields (velocityZoneEmphasis, cueRhythmProfile, metricAnnouncementFrequency, commandVocabularyStyle, visualLeadTimeMs) plus `commandVocabularyStyle` duplicating `voiceVocabulary` with a third 'mixed' value nothing reads, plus a `@deprecated cadenceProfile` that is still the only field the generator's BPM comes from. The recipe type advertises capabilities the engine does not have.

The corpus is duplicated as a .json source of truth and a hand-unreadable `as const satisfies` .ts mirror, with no generator script referenced in the header and no test asserting the two agree. The .ts mirror also drops `notation.tokenNames`, `designStats` and `tierCriteria` (including each tier's `maxExactComboLength` 4/6/9, which GR02 restates and nothing enforces).

Dead function with visibly suspect logic: `headAfterBody` tests `/b/.test(firstSegment) === false && notation.indexOf('b') < notation.length - 2`, mixing a segment test with a raw string-index test, and 'co-square' requires digits.length>=4 plus the set {1,2,3,4} regardless of order. Nothing calls it, so the bug is latent rather than live.

The docstring states 'the opener carrying a two-measure setup pad … k sections fill exactly when their chunks sum to bpm − 2k', but `roundBudget`'s default is `i > 0 ? SETUP_GAP_MEASURES : 0` — the opener gets 0 unless an explicit `setupMeasures` is authored. The stated arithmetic silently depends on data, not on the code it describes.

`const jab = recipe.enabledPunches[0] ?? 1` treats array position as semantics. With `enabledPunches: [3, 4]` the cooldown shadow-boxes lead hooks and still calls the round 'Warm-up'/'Cool down'; the generator has no concept of 'the lightest enabled strike'.

timing.summary: The timing subsystem is a two-layer stack with a clean seam and a lot of dormant scaffolding. Layer 1 is the LIVE path that actually drives a workout: `WorkoutSessionClock` (phase machine + the frozen-on-pause `workElapsedMs` clock) → `expandTimeline` (beats→ms once, at load) → `CueEngine.tick(workElapsedMs)` (cue lifecycle + `token-due`) → `LiveCueMatcher` → `cueScoring`, with coach audio placed by `RhythmMap` (compiled per round) and, for the shipped click-track samples, by the runner's own click-script schedule built from `callPlacement.ts`. Layer 2 is the M39-V2 "one score" stack — `TimingEngine` (960-tick transport), `programCueBridge` → `compileCue` → `workoutScore` → `SlotDispatcher`, plus `MetronomeTransport`/`SharedTransportAnchor` — which is wired but only partly load-bearing: the compiled score drives combo-announce dispatch and the avatar's transport anchor, while rings/scoring still run off the session clock in milliseconds. The ring walk has moved onto the UI thread (`SharedWorkClock` + `useRingBeatClock` + `beatOrdinalAtMs`) as a pure projection, which is the fix for the 2026-08-31 catch-up-burst strobe. Several whole modules are dead at runtime: `acceptance.ts`/`scheduleCombination`/swing, the RhythmMap phrase-placement + cadence-rail branch, and `PacingEngine`'s cadence actions. All 180 tests in `src/domain/timing`, `src/domain/session`, `CueEngine`, `scoreClock` and `beatProjection` pass as of 2026-11-24.

keyFiles.role: The 60-BPM master-pulse doctrine + 960-tick transport math. LIVE exports: TRANSPORT_TICKS_PER_PULSE=960, ticksPerUnit, tickAt, msAtTick, callSlotDurationMs, types BeatDivision/CoachTempo/VoicePolicy. DEAD exports (tests only): stepOffsetMs, scheduleCombination, RhythmicCombination, density, plannedPacePerMinute, combinationDurationMs, callSlotsPerMinute, SWING_* .

Reaction-window constants (EXPECTED_STRIKE_DELAY_MS=140, ACCEPT_FROM_MS=60, ACCEPT_UNTIL_BASE_MS=400, acceptUntilMsFor: div3=450, div4=500). Consumed ONLY by TimingEngine.scheduleCombination, which nothing at runtime calls. The real runtime acceptance windows come from CueTimeline's graces.

Worklet-safe mirror of the SESSION work clock. sharedWorkElapsedMs(clock, frameTimestampMs) = workElapsedAtPublishMs + (frame - publishFrameTimestampMs) when running, else frozen. SHARED_WORK_CLOCK_STOPPED has roundIndex -1. The 'worklet' directive on line ~96 is load-bearing (red screen without it).

Worklet-safe mirror of the METRONOME transport (NOT the session clock). sharedAnchorCurrentTick = anchorTick + elapsedMs*ticksPerMillisecond; ticksPerMillisecondFor(bpm) = bpm*960/60000. Drives the avatar flip clock only.
The injected clock port: now() + schedule(). systemMonotonicClock() prefers performance.now(). Used for *ActualMs stamps and suspension spans — never to decide whether a cue is due.

Phase machine (idle/countdown/work/rest/paused/completed/cancelled) and the authoritative workElapsedMs. Accumulates per-phase deltas in advance(); pause accumulates nothing (that's why CueEngine needs no offset math). enterWork seeds phaseElapsedMs AND workElapsedMs with the overflow. DEFAULT_COUNTDOWN_MS=5000. skipRest()/skipCountdown() only act inside their own phase.
Rest presentation sub-phases (REST_RECOVERY_FRACTION=0.2, REST_PREVIEW_FRACTION=0.75) and RoundResultFreeze, which closes a round's numbers at the bell.

expandTimeline(workout, defaultStance, bpm, options) — ALL beat math, stance resolution, repeat expansion and window clamping happen here once. Emits CueInstance[] per round in plain ms. Sequence stride = comboSpanMs + gapMs per repeatIndex. truncateWindowsAtNextCue() caps each window at the next cue's scheduledStartMs.

Walks a RoundTimeline against workElapsedMs. Statuses queued→previewing→announcing→active→accepting→(completed|expired)→gap. Emits token-due per non-rest token. assertWindowsClamped() in the constructor throws rather than re-clamping. closeOverlapping() ends any in-flight cue when a new one goes active; assertSingleActive() throws if two are active.

Cue lifecycle types, CueTimestamps (scheduled in work-elapsed ms, actual in monotonic ms), CueEvent union including token-due with repId/strikeId, TERMINAL_STATUSES = {completed, expired, gap, cancelled}.

beatsToMs(beats,bpm) = beats*60000/bpm (deliberately fractional), tokenOffsetsMs, maxBeatOffset, blockDurationMs, CADENCE_PROFILES, and bpmForRecipe() — the single seam that chooses legacy nominalBpm vs baseBpm*division*globalSpeed.

beatOrdinalAtMs(scheduledStartMs, tokenOffsetsMs, expectedTokenIndexes, workElapsedMs) → punch ordinal or -1. Pure projection, never an accumulator — this is the structural fix for the catch-up-burst strobe. Carries a 'worklet' directive.

The whole round's bar plan is staged ONCE per round into shared arrays; a useFrameCallback worklet walks it by clock (`while (idx+1<n && elapsed >= s[idx+1]) idx++`). Effect is keyed on [roundIndex, barCount, clock] only, deliberately.
beatOrdinalAtMsWorklet — hand-mirror of beatOrdinalAtMs, pinned by src/components/workout/__tests__/ringBeatWorklet.test.ts.

compileRoundRhythmMap(round, opts) — one compiled coach schedule per round (call / refire / set-callout / instruction / phase-announce / encouragement). Holds most of the coach timing constants. The phrase-placement + cadence-rail branch is unreachable at runtime (see gotchas).

compileRoundSpine(round) → SpineSchedule{beats, pulses, audio, compiled}. beatsFor() builds TokenBeat[] (ring atMs, audioAtMs, audioEndMs, avatarFrameMs); pulsesFor() fills count-scored windows the engine leaves dark; pulseCursorAt() is the count-scored ring cursor.

The ONE place CueInstance → ProgramCue. Site of the 'one grid' fix (GH #305): strike placement now comes from ticksAtMs(cue.tokenOffsetsMs[i]) with atStep kept only as the compiler's fallback. BASE_BPM=60, MS_PER_TRANSPORT_TICK=1.041666…, CADENCE_TO_DIVISION {technical:1, steady:2, pressure:3, sprint:4}, default division 2.

ProgramCue → CompiledCueTimeline. Expands reps, three-level strike ids `${cueId}:${repId}:${strikeIndex}`, compiles BOTH vocabulary tracks, stamps a TimelineIdentity. startTick honours authored.atTick over atStep*unitTicks; targetStrikeTick = startTick + round((endTick-startTick)/2); DEFAULT_RESPONSE_GAP_TICKS=60.

compileWorkoutScore → CompiledWorkoutScore (strikes, coachSlots, phaseBoundaries, FNV-1a timelineHash). Cumulative score-tick axis: rest is NOT represented, so round R starts at sum of prior workDurationTicks. DEFAULT_PRELOAD_MARGIN_TICKS=300.

The only module that knows the score's tick axis is cumulative while workElapsedMs is round-relative. roundStartTicksFrom(score) reads round-start boundaries; scoreTickAt(roundStartTicks, workElapsedMs, roundIndex). MS_PER_SCORE_TICK = 60000/(60*960).

Tick-driven, append-only global coach queue. dispatchAt = reservationStartTick - latencyTicks; currentRoundIndex clamps dispatch (future-round slots are HELD and re-queued in a finally, past-round slots dropped as 'round-elapsed'); play() returning false re-queues until desiredAudibleEndTick then 'retry-expired'.

The unwrapped absolute-tick clock. start() bumps generation and resets tick to 0; pause freezes; correct() applies bounded phase correction with PHASE_CORRECTION_LARGE_TICKS=500 / PHASE_CORRECTION_MAX_STEP_TICKS=20 and NEVER snaps backwards (the clamp that cut the anchor storm from ~300-400/round to 4-12/round); notifyDisruption() preserves the tick but bumps generation.
Reconstructs the absolute tick from a wrapped expo-audio playlist position using JS monotonic time as a coarse anchor. Correct only while JS↔audio skew < half a loop (500 ms on a 1 s loop).
bindSharedTransportAnchor publishes whole-struct atomic updates on every transport transition, plus one initial publish on bind. Frame-timestamp domain = performance.now().

The real runtime call/lead-in placement for the shipped click-track workouts. breathForBar() formula, callDispatchAtMs(), leadInDispatchAtMs(). Holds LEAD_IN_PAD_MS, CALL_PAD_MS, CALL_DISPATCH_LAG_MS, the vocab leads, DENSE_BREATH_MS, MIN_BREATH_MS, DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS, CALL_BREATH_OVERRIDES.

2311 lines; the single 50 ms setInterval that wires everything: session.advance() → applyTransitions → engine.tick(workElapsedMs) → announcer.onTick → slotDispatcher.advance(scoreTickAt(...)) → click-script lead-in/call dispatch → metronome swaps → syncFromEngine → pushStore → viz flush. Also owns TICK_INTERVAL_MS=50, AVATAR_LEAD_MS=375, STORE_THROTTLE_MS=250, METRONOME_SWAP_LEAD_MS=400, PREVIEW_LEAD_REPS=2, audibleDivisionForSlot(), maskedBarIds(), and the SharedWorkClock publish.

compileWorkoutScript — the plan-time, serializable dispatch script (coach.play / coach.phrase / ring.tokenDue / ceremony / bell) the analysis harness diffs captures against. Bell entries are idealized at atMs 0 and atMs = round.workDurationMs. DEFAULT_PER_WORD_ESTIMATE_MS=500, DEFAULT_INTER_CUE_RELEASE_GRACE_MS=50.

CLICK_MAPS — the authored source of all real timing. Per-workout bpm (85/100/120), 4- or 8-slot bars, rate 1|1.5|2, reps, setupMeasures. clickSpecs() lowers a row to a BlockSpec with offsets at 1/rate beats and gapBeats = breathBeats(slots,rate) + step. SETUP_GAP_MEASURES=2, MAX_BURST_PUNCHES_PER_SEC=4, MAX_SUSTAINED_PUNCHES_PER_SEC=2.5.
The 14 rendered click loops. Only (baseBpm, division) pairs 60×{1,2,3,4}, 100×{1,2,3}, 85×{1,2,3} exist — there is NO baseBpm 120 loop. metronomeLoopFor falls back to straight swing then undefined.

Bounded ring buffer for token/avatar/clock transitions, flushed as one batched log line. CLOCK_ANOMALY_MS=250, FLUSH_BATCH=64, MAX_BUFFERED=512, FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS=500. Exists because logging per transition IS the stall.

The call-vs-ring bench. Its 'Runtime status — READ FIRST (2026-09-07)' section is the authoritative statement that the cadence rail is NOT engaged at runtime. Names the measurement loop (tools/analysis/observed-timing.mjs).

Historical root-cause doc for the 'interfering maps' bug. STALE: the `visualOffsetsMs ?? phraseTokenTimesMs ?? tokenOffsetsMs` chain and the proposed src/domain/programs/tokenOffsets.ts never shipped / were retired.

keyConcepts.name: workElapsedMs is the one authority clock
keyConcepts.detail: Round-relative, frozen while paused, reset to the phase overflow on every work-entered. Every scheduling decision (CueEngine.tick, announcer.onTick, click-script dispatch, slotDispatcher via scoreTickAt) compares against this single sample taken once per 50 ms tick. The monotonic clock is written only into *ActualMs fields. A pause therefore needs no offset shifting anywhere — settled decision, explicitly marked 'do not re-litigate'.

keyConcepts.name: beat → ms conversion
keyConcepts.detail: beatsToMs(beats, bpm) = (beats * 60_000) / bpm, fractional on purpose (rounding accumulates over a 3-minute round; callers round at the display/scheduling edge). tokenOffsetsMs maps each WorkoutToken.beatOffset through it, index-preserving. msToBeats is the inverse.

keyConcepts.name: bpmForRecipe — the one tempo seam
keyConcepts.detail: metronome.enabled false → CADENCE_PROFILES[recipe.cadenceProfile].nominalBpm. metronome.enabled true → coachTempo.baseBpm * coachTempo.division * globalSpeed. Every compiler (expandTimeline, workoutScore, workoutScript) takes 'just a bpm'.

keyConcepts.name: CADENCE_PROFILES
keyConcepts.detail: technical {80,90,nominal 85}, steady {95,110,100}, pressure {110,130,120}, sprint {130,150,140}. clampToProfile(bpm, profile) is the hard stop for PacingEngine's ±10-15%.

keyConcepts.name: Beat divisions = one clock, four subdivisions
keyConcepts.detail: Division 1 technical = 1000 ms/slot = 60 slots/min; 2 flow/steady = 500 ms = 120; 3 pressure/triplet = 333 ms = 180; 4 sprint = 250 ms = 240 — all at baseBpm 60. divisionForCadenceProfile maps the legacy profile names to 1/2/3/4.

keyConcepts.name: TRANSPORT_TICKS_PER_PULSE = 960
keyConcepts.detail: 960 ticks per master pulse ≈ 1.0416666 ms/tick at 60 BPM. Divides cleanly by every division (960/480/320/240) and by the 12-step authoring grid (TICKS_PER_AUTHORING_STEP = 80). V1c used 12 and was too coarse for the ±10-15 ms fit check. No other file is allowed to hardcode 12 or 960.

keyConcepts.name: MS_PER_TRANSPORT_TICK / ticksAtMs
keyConcepts.detail: 60_000 / (60 * 960) = 1.0416666… ms. ticksAtMs(ms) = Math.round(ms / that). Defined identically and independently in three places: programCueBridge.ts:85, workoutScore.ts:75, scoreClock.ts:29 (named MS_PER_SCORE_TICK).

keyConcepts.name: Cue lead times
keyConcepts.detail: DEFAULT_PREVIEW_LEAD_MS = 1_500 (previewAt = max(0, start-1500)); DEFAULT_ANNOUNCE_LEAD_MS = 750 (announceAt = max(0, start-750)); CueEngine's DEFAULT_LEAD_TIMES = {previewMs: 1_500, announceMs: 750, readyToneMs: 100}. readyToneMs fires a 'cue-ready' event but NO tone is ever compiled — RhythmMap explicitly refuses ready tones ('no beeps, ever'); it survives only as the quiet margin a phrase must finish inside.

keyConcepts.name: The REAL acceptance window
keyConcepts.detail: windowStartMs = min(workDurationMs, max(0, scheduledStartMs - DEFAULT_GRACE_BEFORE_MS=200)); windowEndMs = min(workDurationMs, scheduledEndMs + DEFAULT_GRACE_AFTER_MS=350); then truncateWindowsAtNextCue caps it at next.scheduledStartMs (floored at the cue's own windowStartMs). Asymmetric on purpose: late is ordinary, early was not a response to the cue. Per-block overrides via block.graceBeforeMs/graceAfterMs.

keyConcepts.name: The 200 ms window overlap is structural
keyConcepts.detail: Because windowStart opens 200 ms before scheduledStartMs while the previous cue's window is truncated AT that same scheduledStartMs, cue-window-opened(N) always arrives BEFORE cue-window-closed(P). LiveCueMatcher.onCueEvent is cue-id-keyed for exactly this reason; an unkeyed single slot orphaned the matcher after a round's first cue (2026-08-31).

keyConcepts.name: Window clamping is asserted, not re-derived
keyConcepts.detail: assertWindowsClamped() runs over the whole timeline in the CueEngine constructor and THROWS if windowStartMs < 0 or windowEndMs > round.workDurationMs. Quietly correcting there would hide broken expansion and let events be accepted during rest.

keyConcepts.name: Cue lifecycle + the big-tick loop
keyConcepts.detail: advance() runs step() in a `for(;;)` until the status stops changing, so one large tick can carry a cue through several states (a dropped frame must not strand it). fireDueTokens caps `until = Math.min(t, cue.windowEndMs)` so a coarse tick fires exactly the tokens a fine one would — tick-size invariance is pinned by ~60 seeded-timeline tests and must not be 'fixed'.

keyConcepts.name: token-due dedupe is by strikeId, not tokenIndex
keyConcepts.detail: firedTokens is a Set<string> of strikeIdFor(cueId, DEFAULT_REP_ID='rep-0', tokenIndex) = `${cueId}:rep-0:${i}`, migrated from Set<number> so the two 1s in 1-1-2 are distinguishable. Rest tokens return early and emit nothing (they would inject phantom ring events into the cadence-lab drift signal and viz forensics).

keyConcepts.name: CueScoring: sequence vs count
keyConcepts.detail: SEQUENCE_KINDS = exact-combo, repeated-combo, defense-counter, footwork-exit → one cue per repeatIndex, matched token by token. COUNT_SCORED_KINDS = volume-burst, open-pressure, coast, active-recovery → ONE cue spanning the block, expectedPunches = [], judged on counted >= targetPunches; DEFAULT_BURST_COUNTDOWN_MS = 3_000. Anything else lands in deferredBlockIds.

keyConcepts.name: Rings vs matcher use different index spaces
keyConcepts.detail: token-due carries a TOKEN index over all tokens (defense/footwork/coach included; only 'rest' skipped). beatOrdinalAtMs returns a PUNCH ORDINAL over expectedPunches. The ring walk and the engine's event stream are therefore not index-comparable.

keyConcepts.name: 'One grid' fix (GH #305)
keyConcepts.detail: Before it, programCueBridge emitted only `atStep: ordinal`, and compileCue placed strikes at atStep * unitTicks — tempo-BLIND, so every strike sat 500 ms apart at every workout tempo (measured identical at 85 and 240 BPM across all ten samples) while the rings ran tempo-scaled tokenOffsetsMs; the two grids diverged by up to 867 ms. Fix: optional atTick/endAtTick on AuthoredStrike filled from ticksAtMs(tokenOffsetsMs[i]); ring↔score agreement is now ≤0.98 ms. A strike's endAtTick is the next strike's tick; the last reuses the previous gap. Only a cross-tempo RATIO test catches this class — 38 ordering/bounds tests all passed under the bug.

keyConcepts.name: Score ticks are cumulative; workElapsedMs is round-relative
keyConcepts.detail: compileWorkoutScore walks one cursorTick across rounds (round 0 at 0, round 1 at 230400, round 2 at 460800 ticks = 240 s rounds), and rest is NOT represented in the axis. Feeding workElapsedMs straight into SlotDispatcher.advance addressed only round 0's band, dumped all of round 1 in one tick at the end of round 0, then never reached rounds 2+. scoreTickAt(roundStartTicks, workElapsedMs, roundIndex) is the lift; an unknown round contributes 0 rather than throwing.

keyConcepts.name: SlotDispatcher round band (precall bleed)
keyConcepts.detail: Because the score axis has no rest gap, a round's opening announce authored to LEAD its bell (speed-combos round 1: −2355 ms, absolute tick 228139 in a round-0 band ending at 230400) fired 2.7 s before the round-0 bell. currentRoundIndex now HOLDS future-round slots (re-queued in a `finally` so a throw cannot strand them) and DROPS past-round slots as 'round-elapsed'.

keyConcepts.name: Never snap the visual clock backwards
keyConcepts.detail: MetronomeTransport.correct(): |error| < PHASE_CORRECTION_LARGE_TICKS=500 and error > 0 → slew anchor forward by min(error, PHASE_CORRECTION_MAX_STEP_TICKS=20), no notify. error < 0 → hold, always. |error| >= 500 and error < 0 → hold (summarised log at most 1/s; a baseBpm/loop mismatch produced ~500 holds/sec). |error| >= 500 and error > 0 → hard re-anchor + generation bump + notify. The backwards clamp is what cut the anchor storm from ~300-400 re-anchors/round to 4-12.

keyConcepts.name: SharedWorkClock is published only at discontinuities
keyConcepts.detail: The runner re-anchors it inside applyTransitions on every transition (work-entered with its overflow, paused, resumed, rest-entered) and NEVER per tick, so the UI thread owns smoothness between anchors. running is `phase === 'work'` only. Deliberately NOT the transport anchor: the rings run the SESSION clock on every workout, the transport only on metronome.enabled ones.

keyConcepts.name: Ring walk v3 — whole round staged, worklet walks by clock
keyConcepts.detail: Two earlier designs died: adopt-what-JS-calls-current (bars promoted 60-600 ms late) and stage-one-successor-ahead (engine flipped current faster than boundary promotes consumed it; captured stages #35..#39 in 5 s then promote #38, bars #34-37 never walked). Now JS stages the entire round's bars once and the worklet does `while (idx+1<n && elapsed >= s[idx+1]) idx++`; a cold/late join SNAPS (option-C: never replay what is over).

keyConcepts.name: Click-script call placement formula
keyConcepts.detail: breathForBar: breathMs = max(MIN_BREATH_MS + DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS, min(dense, dense − BREATH_TRACK_GAIN * max(0, slotMs − BREATH_REF_SLOT_MS))), with CALL_BREATH_OVERRIDES[slot] winning outright. dispatchAtMs = max(0, firstNodeMs − clipDurationMs − breathMs − CALL_DISPATCH_LAG_MS). Lead-in: dispatchAtMs = max(0, endByMs − clipDurationMs − LEAD_IN_PAD_MS − leadMs), where endByMs is the rep-0 CALL's dispatch time (not the first strike) — anchoring to the strike was ~2 s of permanent false WARN in the correlator.

keyConcepts.name: Call-placement constant values
keyConcepts.detail: LEAD_IN_PAD_MS=250, CALL_PAD_MS=500, CALL_DISPATCH_LAG_MS=71 (measured: 46.5 ms scheduler lateness + 25.0 ms play()→audio), TECHNIQUE_CALL_LEAD_MS=250, TECHNIQUE_LEADIN_LEAD_MS=500, NUMBERS_CALL_LEAD_MS=100, DENSE_BREATH_MS={numbers:600, techniques:750}, BREATH_REF_SLOT_MS=300, BREATH_TRACK_GAIN=1.0, MIN_BREATH_MS=150, DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS=95, CALL_BREATH_OVERRIDES={'call/1-.-.-.':340, 'call/1-.-2-.':340}.

keyConcepts.name: RhythmMap coach-timing constants
keyConcepts.detail: DEFAULT_ANNOUNCE_LEAD_TIMES {announceMs:750, readyToneMs:100}; BURST_REFIRE_INTERVAL_MS=6_000, MIN_BURST_MS_FOR_REFIRE=10_000, BURST_TAIL_QUIET_MS=1_500; PHASE_MARKS=[0.5,0.83]; INSTRUCTION_START_PAD_MS=250; SET_CALLOUT_QUIET_MS=500, SET_CALLOUT_PART_GAP_MS=450 (widened from 250 after parts stacked under tick jitter), SET_CALLOUT_MIN_CLEAR_MS=200, ROUND_OPEN_QUIET_MS=1_500; CLOSER_AT_REMAINING_MS=30_000, CLOSER_SEARCH_BACK_MS=4_000, 13-entry CLOSER_ROTATION; REANNOUNCE_MIN_CLEAR_MS=150, PER_TOKEN_PHRASE_ESTIMATE_MS=500; ENCOURAGEMENT_GAP_MS=15_000, MAX_ENCOURAGEMENTS_PER_ROUND=6; POWER_MAX_TOKENS=2, POWER_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=5_000, POWER_MIN_REPS=3, POWER_STRIKES_MS=1_800, MAX_POWER_ANNOUNCES_PER_ROUND=2; RAIL_K_MS=120.

keyConcepts.name: Cadence rail contract
keyConcepts.detail: 'Ring N lights RAIL_K_MS (120 ms) after word N's audible envelope ends.' Placement: railStartAt = cue.scheduledStartMs − RAIL_K_MS − word0.endOffsetMs, used only if railStartAt >= cue.previewAt; otherwise the classic rule startAt = max(previewAt, (scheduledStartMs − readyToneMs) − lengthMs − phraseShift). RhythmSpine inverts it: audioEndMs = atMs − RAIL_K_MS, audioAtMs = audioEndMs − (word.endMs − word.onsetMs).

keyConcepts.name: Round transitions and the bell
keyConcepts.detail: WorkoutSessionClock.advancePhase: work → rest (phaseElapsedMs = overflow) unless it's the last round with rest<=0 (→ complete) or rest<=0 (→ enterWork(next, overflow)); rest → enterWork(next, overflow) or complete. The runner's applyTransitions then, per transition: publishes the SharedWorkClock, logs puncheokie.round.boundary, and on work-entered rebuilds walk plan / lead-in schedule / avatar track / metronome schedule, installs the round's rhythm map, and starts the metronome; on rest-entered freezes the round result, stops the metronome and calls voice.output.cancel(AUDIO_PRIORITY.bell). The bell itself is a voice ASSET played by CueAnnouncer.onSessionPhase on work-entered, rest-entered and finishing (same ding-ding both ends; the gong is retired).

keyConcepts.name: Pause / resume semantics, layer by layer
keyConcepts.detail: Session: pause() just flips phase; resume() sets lastAdvanceAtMs = now so the paused interval is discarded, never accumulated. CueEngine: paused || trackerFault → isSuspended(); tick() returns early; SUSPENDABLE = {announcing, active, accepting} go to 'suspended' with priorStatus saved and a monotonic suspension span pushed. Transport: pause() freezes anchorAbsoluteTick, resume() re-anchors monotonic, generation unchanged — but the RUNNER treats pause as a hard metronome stop() and resume as a fresh start() (so the click lands back on the downbeat), which DOES bump generation. CueAnnouncer cancels everything below AUDIO_PRIORITY.safety on pause.

keyConcepts.name: Scoring windows ≠ acceptance windows
keyConcepts.detail: TIMING_TIGHT_MS = 150 decides 'was it on the beat' (timingWindowPct, and the runner's onTimeForMatch haptic gate against cue.scheduledStartMs + tokenOffsetsMs[tokenIndex]). The acceptance window (200/350 + truncation) decides whether the punch belongs to the cue at all.

keyConcepts.name: Runner loop constants
keyConcepts.detail: TICK_INTERVAL_MS=50, STORE_THROTTLE_MS=250 (was 100; 10 Hz re-render churn starved the JS responder and made Pressables dead during work), RECENT_EVENT_WINDOW=256, AVATAR_LEAD_MS=375 (tuned down from 750; next stop 250), PREVIEW_LEAD_REPS=2, METRONOME_SWAP_LEAD_MS=400. Measured on-tablet the interval actually fires at ~150-341 ms under load, so backlogs are routine.

keyConcepts.name: Countdown is a CAP, not a fixed lead-in
keyConcepts.detail: live.tsx passes countdownMs = intro.totalMs + INTRO_COUNTDOWN_SLACK_MS (1_500) when the voice is on; intro.totalMs = sum(gapBeforeMs + durationMs) + INTRO_TAIL_PAD_MS (900), with INTRO_SEGMENT_GAP_MS = 350 between segments. skipCountdown() rings the first bell as soon as the walkout lands rather than serving the slack in silence.

keyConcepts.name: Measure arithmetic in the click maps
keyConcepts.detail: A measure = 4 beats. At rate r a slot = 1/r beat. Stride table: 4-slot@1x = 2 m/rep, 4-slot@1.5x = 1 m, 4-slot@2x = 1 m, 8-slot@1x = 3 m, 8-slot@2x = 1.5 m. gapBeats = breathBeats(slots,rate) + step, where the `+ step` carries the final slot's own width — without it every rep laid one slot short, rounds under-filled ~12% and ended with ~30 s of dead air before the bell (caught 2026-09-02).

gotchas: The task brief's example constant is WRONG: LEAD_IN_PAD_MS is 250, in src/domain/coach/callPlacement.ts:38 — not 282, and not in VoicePolicy.ts. It WAS briefly 282 (commit ea5df336) and was reverted in 1af8a232 because the paired DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS 95→127 bump caused cross-workout regressions (quick-uppercut-lane −113.5 ms on call/1-2-5-2 r0, establish-the-jab-20 −32.5 ms, switch-by-round −24.7 ms; 4 FAIL / 1 ERROR / 17 WARN / 0 PASS across the 24-workout suite). Do not re-tune either as a global constant; use CALL_BREATH_OVERRIDES.

src/domain/timing/acceptance.ts is DEAD at runtime. EXPECTED_STRIKE_DELAY_MS=140 / ACCEPT_FROM_MS=60 / ACCEPT_UNTIL_BASE_MS=400 / acceptUntilMsFor(3)=450 / acceptUntilMsFor(4)=500 are consumed only by TimingEngine.scheduleCombination, which has no caller outside src/domain/timing/__tests__. The acceptance windows that actually gate matching are DEFAULT_GRACE_BEFORE_MS=200 / DEFAULT_GRACE_AFTER_MS=350 in CueTimeline plus truncateWindowsAtNextCue. Two unrelated acceptance models coexist; changing acceptance.ts changes nothing on glass.

The whole 'swing' + RhythmicCombination half of TimingEngine is dead too: stepOffsetMs, SWING_EVEN/ROLLING/SINGSONG/MAX, density, plannedPacePerMinute, callSlotsPerMinute, combinationDurationMs(combo), scheduleCombination, ScheduledPunch — no non-test importer. Swing survives only as a WAV-selection key in metronomeAssets, and every shipped sample authors swing 0.5.

The '60 BPM master pulse' doctrine is NOT what runs. Every shipped sample sets metronome.enabled: true and either coachTempo {baseBpm: MAP.bpm, division: 1} (body-work 100, progressive-buildup 100, pump-and-coast 100, establish-the-jab-20 100, switch-by-round 85, uppercut-clinic 85) or {baseBpm: 60, division: 2} (three-round-fundamentals, heavy-hands, speed-combos, pace-pusher — whose maps are all bpm 120, so 60×2 = 120 by coincidence). So bpmForRecipe returns 85/100/120, and the visual grid runs there, while compileCue/workoutScore/programCueBridge hardcode BASE_BPM = 60 for the TICK axis. Two different senses of 'bpm' in one subsystem.

The cadence RAIL is not engaged at runtime. The runner passes `wordMarksFor: () => undefined` and `phraseShiftFor: () => undefined` (_useWorkoutRunner.ts:477-478 and again at 1719), and VoiceOutputExpo.combinationDurationMs() unconditionally returns undefined (Phase 5-iv retired the per-punch phrase corpus). So RhythmMap ALWAYS takes the per-word branch: the entire `lengthMs !== undefined` block (rail placement, finishBy, phraseShift, phrase-mode call events) is unreachable, and rings are on the beat grid everywhere. Word onsets/ends still exist for 562 of 776 clips in phraseTimingManifest.ts. Read .claude/skills/cadence-lab/SKILL.md 'Runtime status — READ FIRST' before diagnosing any drift report as a rail failure.

PacingEngine proposes but nothing applies. The runner calls pacingRef.current.onBoundary('rest', …) and pushes an AdaptationRecord, but only decision.cueText is consumed (pacingCueRef → store). The timeline is useMemo'd on [workout, stance, bpm] and expandTimeline is never re-run mid-session, so a 'cadence-scale' / 'gap-scale' / 'reallocate' action is inert. Much of CueTimeline's clamping rationale ('PacingEngine's ±10-15% adjustment does exactly that, and the shipped samples overlap at 85 BPM today') describes a path that cannot currently fire.

Doc D20 says 'Timing is no longer scored' and timingWindowPct is retired, but cueScoring.ts still computes and aggregates timingWindowPct (lines 56, 164, 226, 246, 254) against TIMING_TIGHT_MS. The doc (docs/design-spec.md) and the code disagree. Related: D18 says credit is on order and hand 'at any point while the Set is presenting' — LiveCueMatcher honours that (its comment says 'Credit is presence, not arithmetic (D18)'), while CueMatcher still has a 'window' gate that LiveCueMatcher must call with gate:'open' to avoid manufacturing a correction on every set.

expandCountScoredBlock clamps windowStartMs with only `Math.max(0, …)` while expandBlock also clamps it with `Math.min(ctx.workDurationMs, …)`. A count-scored block scheduled past the bell therefore gets windowStartMs > windowEndMs — an inverted window — and assertWindowsClamped only tests `windowStartMs < 0 || windowEndMs > workDurationMs`, so it will not catch it. Compare CueTimeline.ts:412-425 against 485-486.

CueEngine.fireDueTokens publishes token-due for EVERY non-rest token, including defense / footwork / coach tokens (only `kind === 'rest'` returns early). Anything consuming token-due as 'a punch happened' must filter by token kind itself.

CueEngine.tick ignores a backwards tick and returns early while suspended WITHOUT updating lastTickMs — so snapshot().remainingMs and repeatCue() read a frozen lastTickMs during a pause. That is intended, but loadRound resets lastTickMs to -1, so the first tick of a round can be any value.

The runner publishes the SharedWorkClock inside the per-transition loop but reads `sessionRef.current.snapshot()` each time — and session.advance() has already applied ALL transitions before applyTransitions runs. So when one advance crosses two boundaries (rest-entered + work-entered), both iterations publish the same final snapshot. Harmless today only because the final state is the one that matters.

metronomeAssets has NO baseBpm 120 loop. Only (60, {1,2,3,4}), (100, {1,2,3}) and (85, {1,2,3}) are rendered. Nothing currently requests 120 because the 120-BPM maps use coachTempo.baseBpm 60 with division 2 — but any recipe that sets baseBpm: 120 will get `metronomeLoopFor` → undefined, a `puncheokie.metronome 'no loop for tempo'` warn, and the transport will never start (which also freezes the avatar flip clock, since it rides SharedTransportAnchor). This is exactly the bug class that left the avatar frozen on 7 of 11 workouts.

Only a cross-TEMPO ratio test catches the tempo-blindness bug class. 38 ordering/bounds tests passed while the compiled score sat on a fixed 500 ms lattice. When touching compileCue/programCueBridge placement, assert that strike spacing SCALES with bpm, not just that it is ordered.

vizForensics is instrumentation that must not perturb what it measures (M39-V2 principle #18). It buffers and flushes one batched log line at the END of the runner tick (FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS=500, FLUSH_BATCH=64, MAX_BUFFERED=512) and only records clock records on anomalies (CLOCK_ANOMALY_MS=250). Do not add per-transition logger.info calls to the token/ring path — a measured baseBpm/loop mismatch produced ~500 transport-hold logs/sec and red-screened the JS thread, which is why MetronomeTransport.correct summarises at 1 Hz.

The 'worklet' directive placement is load-bearing and non-obvious: it lives at the CALL SITE for sharedAnchorCurrentTick, but INSIDE the function for sharedWorkElapsedMs and beatOrdinalAtMs/beatOrdinalAtMsWorklet. Missing it yields '[Worklets] Tried to synchronously call a Remote Function on the UI Runtime' — an instant red screen on device that jest cannot see (jest runs everything on one thread).

Per the Metro-watcher memory note: there is no fast refresh on F:. Every edit batch to this subsystem needs a Metro restart plus an app cold-restart to reach the tablet, so iterate through the pure domain tests (`npx jest src/domain/timing src/domain/session src/domain/programs`) before driving on glass.

docs/v1c-ring-avatar-sync-plan.md is a stale plan, not a description of the code. The `visualOffsetsMs ?? phraseTokenTimesMs ?? tokenOffsetsMs` authority chain and the proposed src/domain/programs/tokenOffsets.ts do not exist; CueInstance carries neither field (retired in V2 Phase 5-ii). CueEngine.fireDueTokens reads cue.tokenOffsetsMs directly.

smells.concern: RAIL_K_MS = 120 is DUPLICATED in both files, each with a comment claiming it is 'one constant so the spine, the announcer's rail-placement math and any mic-anchored analyzer share it'. They do not share it; nothing imports the other's copy. The cadence-lab skill treats 120 as THE contract, so a one-sided edit silently breaks the rail's invertibility (RhythmSpine.audioTimesFor inverts exactly what RhythmMap's placement computed).

The comment says beatsFor 'reads through the shared authority chain visualOffsetsMs ?? phraseTokenTimesMs ?? tokenOffsetsMs via tokenOffsetFor'. The code reads `cue.tokenOffsetsMs[i]` directly and tokenOffsetFor does not exist. The one-grid post-mortem explicitly blames a false doc comment of exactly this shape for letting the 867 ms divergence survive — this is the same failure mode, still present.

Documents the format as `${cueId}:${tokenIndex}` while strikeIdFor actually produces `${cueId}:${repId}:${strikeIndex}` (strikeCatalog.ts:251). CueState.ts:111 documents the three-level form. Anyone parsing strikeIds off this comment will mis-split.

'960 PPQN at 60 BPM = 16 ticks/ms' is arithmetically wrong by ~16.7×: at 60 BPM, ticksPerSecond = 960, i.e. 0.96 ticks/ms (MS_PER_TRANSPORT_TICK ≈ 1.0417 ms). A caller sizing latencyTicks from this comment would compensate 16× too much.

The `lengthMs !== undefined` phrase branch — rail placement, phraseShiftFor, finishBy, phrase-mode call events, the phrase-mode repeat-thinning gate — is unreachable because durationFor always returns undefined. ~100 lines of live-looking scheduling logic that cannot execute, alongside a duplicated thinning gate in the per-word branch. Either wire it (plan C6) or delete it; it currently invites 'fixes' to code that never runs.

Mangled/contradictory comment block: three half-sentences spliced together ('Engine-mode ring times can land past the beat-grid comboSpan; extend windowEndMs to include the last visualOffset so' / 'A cue's window ends at scheduledEndMs plus the grace tail;' / 'per-token engine widening is gone'). The first clause describes behaviour the code no longer has. Also line 488 has stray extra indentation in expandCountScoredBlock's object literal.

combo.totalTicks falls back to `totalSteps * unitTicks` for a lone-strike combo (no second offset to derive a span from), which is the same tempo-blind lattice the one-grid fix removed. It only affects the rep stride, and repetition.count is always 1 from the bridge — so it is dormant, but it is the exact bug that already shipped once. Single-punch coast bars are precisely the family that needed CALL_BREATH_OVERRIDES.

divisionForCue defaults to 2 ('steady') when cue.cadence is absent, independent of the recipe's actual coachTempo.division. For the shipped samples (division 1 at 85/100 BPM) this silently halves unitTicks in compileCue, which still matters for endAtTick/spanSteps fallbacks and for `atStep`-authored patterns. The recipe's real division is never threaded into the bridge.

Throws mid-round if two cues are simultaneously active/accepting, with the message 'The timeline should never overlap cues' — but the file's own closeOverlapping doc explains that overlap IS expected and is handled by closing the earlier cue. The throw is a live crash path guarding an invariant the same class deliberately repairs; the header even records that an earlier version 'threw from tick() when it did, which killed the round'.

smells.where: src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/_useWorkoutRunner.ts (2311 lines, one 2100-line useEffect + a ~160-line setInterval body)
smells.concern: The entire live ordering contract (session → transitions → engine tick → announcer → slotDispatcher → click-script lane → metronome swaps → store push → viz flush) lives inside one interval callback in a React hook module, with ~15 refs for cross-tick state and two eslint-disable'd exhaustive-deps escapes for the clock slots. Nothing outside the app can test the ordering; callPlacement.ts was extracted for exactly this reason and the rest was not.

DELIVERED_BREATH_SHORTFALL_MS and CALL_BREATH_OVERRIDES carry ~100 lines of measurement narrative, a reverted tune, and per-slot magic numbers keyed by motif strings ('call/1-.-2-.'). The clamp-bite thresholds (655 ms numbers / 805 ms techniques) are stated in prose and derived nowhere in code, so they drift the moment MIN_BREATH_MS or DENSE_BREATH_MS moves. There is also a still-open unmeasured PLAYHEAD_TO_SPEAKER_MS acknowledged in the comment.

ticksAtMs / Math.round(ms / MS_PER_TRANSPORT_TICK) is independently re-derived in three modules from three private BASE_BPM = 60 constants, with the comment in each promising it 'matches' the others. One edit desynchronises the score's tick axis from the bridge's strike ticks and from scoreTickAt's runtime lift — and the timelineHash would still agree with itself, so the divergence would be invisible to the identity check.

Two doc comments stacked with no body between them: the 'Close a cue's acceptance window and settle its outcome / Partial completion is not failure' block is immediately followed by the 'Credit a punch to a count-scored cue' block, and the method that lands there is notifyCount, not closeWindow. notifyCount is also a public method wedged between private internals.

tooling.summary: punchCraft is an Android-first Expo 57 / React Native 0.86.2 / TypeScript app (pinned exactly — `.npmrc` sets `save-exact=true`) living at F:/punchCraft, with a very large side-car toolchain under `tools/` (~23k lines of .mjs/.ts/.py) that does voice-clip rendering, unattended on-tablet verification and timing forensics. The CI gate is seven steps (npm ci, typecheck, lint, jest, two custom guards) and I verified all of them pass right now: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, `eslint src --max-warnings 0` exit 0, both guards exit 0, jest 180 suites / 4141 tests / 22 snapshots green in ~190 s. The real working loop is not npm scripts — it is raw `node tools/analysis/*.mjs` invocations driving a release APK on a wirelessly-ADB'd Lenovo tablet via a `punchcraft://qa/run` deep link, judged by `verify-first-round.mjs` (content) and `observed-timing.mjs` (timing), with two local Claude skills (`cadence-lab`, `qa-audio-verify`) encoding the runbooks. The biggest trap for a new session: those two skills, and the plan docs half the tools cite, are NOT in git — `.gitignore:58` ignores `.claude/`, so a fresh clone has neither. Second biggest: several of the authoritative-looking docs (README.md, tools/voice/README.md, docs/audio-validation-rulebook.md, parts of both skills) describe a phrase-clip pipeline that was retired in V2 Phase 5-iv (commit `369a2c6`) and will send you to deprecated or self-refusing tools.
